questions.questionText: A startup wants to avoid large upfront investments in physical servers while it tests a new product idea. Which AWS Cloud economic benefit does this describe?

options.text: Trading capital expense for variable expense
Achieving economies of scale by pooling hardware purchases
Increasing speed and agility of infrastructure provisioning
Stopping the need to guess infrastructure capacity

questions.correctExplanation: Instead of investing heavily in data centers and servers before knowing how they will be used, the company can pay only for the compute resources it consumes, converting capital expenditure into variable operating expenditure.

distractorExplanations.b: Economies of scale describes AWS passing on cost savings from aggregated demand across many customers, not the startup's own spending pattern.
distractorExplanations.c: Speed and agility refers to how quickly new resources can be provisioned, which is a separate benefit from the capital-to-variable expense shift.
distractorExplanations.d: Eliminating capacity guessing refers to elastic scaling to match demand, not the avoidance of upfront investment.

questions.hint: Think about capital expenditure versus operating expenditure.

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes the AWS Cloud benefit of 'economies of scale'?

options.text: AWS aggregates usage from hundreds of thousands of customers, which can lead to lower pay-as-you-go prices over time
Customers can launch resources in minutes instead of weeks
Customers can deploy applications in multiple AWS Regions around the world
Customers only pay for the compute power, storage, and other resources they use

questions.correctExplanation: Because AWS aggregates usage across a very large customer base, it can achieve higher economies of scale, which translates into lower pay-as-you-go prices for customers.

distractorExplanations.b: This describes the agility benefit of rapid provisioning, not economies of scale.
distractorExplanations.c: This describes the benefit of global reach through the AWS global infrastructure.
distractorExplanations.d: This describes the pay-as-you-go pricing benefit rather than economies of scale specifically.

questions.hint: Consider how volume purchasing affects unit pricing.

questions.questionText: Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar focuses on the ability to run and monitor systems to deliver business value and to continually improve supporting processes?
questions.correctExplanation: The Operational Excellence pillar focuses on running and monitoring systems to deliver business value and continually improving processes and procedures.

distractorExplanations.b: Performance Efficiency focuses on using computing resources efficiently and maintaining efficiency as demand changes.
distractorExplanations.c: Reliability focuses on the ability of a workload to perform its intended function correctly and consistently, including recovery from failures.
distractorExplanations.d: Cost Optimization focuses on avoiding unnecessary costs and understanding spending over time.

questions.hint: This pillar is about running, monitoring, and improving processes.

questions.questionText: Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar includes the ability of a workload to recover from infrastructure or service disruptions?
questions.correctExplanation: The Reliability pillar covers a workload's ability to perform its intended function correctly and consistently, including recovering from infrastructure or service disruptions and dynamically acquiring resources to meet demand.

distractorExplanations.b: The Security pillar focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets, not recovery from disruption.
distractorExplanations.c: The Sustainability pillar focuses on minimizing the environmental impact of running workloads.
distractorExplanations.d: Cost Optimization focuses on avoiding unnecessary costs, not resilience.

questions.hint: Think about disaster recovery and fault tolerance.

questions.questionText: A company wants to move an on-premises application to AWS with the least amount of change, simply moving it as-is onto EC2 instances. Which of the '6 R's' migration strategy does this represent?
questions.correctExplanation: Rehosting, often called 'lift and shift,' involves moving applications without making changes to take advantage of the cloud, typically the fastest migration strategy.

distractorExplanations.b: Replatforming ('lift, tinker, and shift') involves making a few cloud optimizations without changing the core application architecture.
distractorExplanations.c: Refactoring (re-architecting) involves reimagining how an application is architected using cloud-native features, which requires significant change.
distractorExplanations.d: Retiring means decommissioning applications that are no longer needed, not moving them to AWS.

questions.hint: This is also known as 'lift and shift'.

questions.questionText: A company runs a large VMware-based environment and wants to move the infrastructure to a cloud version of the platform without purchasing new hardware, rewriting applications, or changing the existing operating model. Which migration strategy best matches this approach?
questions.correctExplanation: Relocate is used when infrastructure and workloads are moved to a cloud version of an existing platform without purchasing new hardware, rewriting applications, or changing the current operational model. It is commonly associated with large-scale platform-level moves such as VMware environments.

distractorExplanations.a: Rehosting moves applications to cloud infrastructure with minimal application changes, but relocation specifically moves an existing platform or infrastructure environment to a cloud version of that platform without changing the operating model.
distractorExplanations.c: Replatforming makes targeted cloud optimizations to an application while preserving its core architecture; the scenario describes moving the existing platform with essentially no application or operational-model changes.
distractorExplanations.d: Refactoring substantially changes application architecture to use cloud-native capabilities, which conflicts with the requirement to avoid rewriting applications.

questions.hint: Look for the strategy that moves an existing platform with minimal change to applications and operations.

questions.questionText: What is the primary difference between cloud computing and traditional on-premises IT infrastructure?

options.text: Cloud computing provides on-demand delivery of IT resources over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing
Cloud computing requires customers to purchase and maintain their own physical servers
Cloud computing eliminates the need for any networking configuration
Cloud computing is only available for large enterprises

questions.correctExplanation: Cloud computing is the on-demand delivery of IT resources over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing, replacing the need to buy, own, and maintain physical data centers and servers.

distractorExplanations.b: This describes traditional on-premises IT, the opposite of cloud computing.
distractorExplanations.c: Networking configuration (VPCs, subnets, route tables) is still required in the cloud, just managed differently.
distractorExplanations.d: Cloud computing is available to organizations of all sizes, including startups and individuals.

questions.hint: Focus on the delivery model and pricing structure.

questions.questionText: Which cloud deployment model involves keeping some resources on-premises while integrating with cloud-based resources?
questions.correctExplanation: A hybrid deployment connects cloud-based resources with existing on-premises infrastructure, often used to extend infrastructure while migrating gradually.

distractorExplanations.b: An all-in (cloud-native) deployment runs applications entirely in the cloud with no on-premises component.
distractorExplanations.c: An on-premises deployment (sometimes called private cloud) uses virtualization and resource management tools locally, without connecting to public cloud resources.
distractorExplanations.d: Private deployment generally refers to on-premises resource management, not a mix with public cloud.

questions.hint: This model bridges two environments.

questions.questionText: A company's workload experiences unpredictable traffic spikes during sales events. Which cloud characteristic allows AWS resources to automatically increase or decrease capacity to match this demand?
questions.correctExplanation: Elasticity is the ability of a system to acquire resources as needed and release resources that are no longer needed, allowing capacity to scale up or down with demand.

distractorExplanations.b: High availability refers to designing systems to minimize downtime, not scaling capacity with demand.
distractorExplanations.c: Fault tolerance is the ability of a system to remain operational even if some components fail.
distractorExplanations.d: Durability refers to data being preserved without loss or corruption over time, not compute scaling.

questions.hint: Think about scaling resources up and down automatically.

questions.questionText: According to the AWS Well-Architected Framework, which pillar addresses using the right amount of resources to meet system requirements and maintaining that efficiency as technology and demand change?
questions.correctExplanation: The Performance Efficiency pillar focuses on using computing resources efficiently to meet system requirements and maintaining that efficiency as demand changes and technologies evolve.

distractorExplanations.b: Operational Excellence focuses on running and monitoring systems and continually improving processes, not resource efficiency itself.
distractorExplanations.c: Security focuses on protecting data, systems, and assets.
distractorExplanations.d: Reliability focuses on a workload consistently performing its intended function, including recovery from failures.

questions.hint: This pillar is about matching resource types and sizes to workload needs.

questions.questionText: Which Well-Architected Framework pillar was added to help customers understand and minimize the environmental impacts of running cloud workloads?
questions.correctExplanation: The Sustainability pillar focuses on minimizing the environmental impacts of running cloud workloads, including energy efficiency and resource usage.

distractorExplanations.b: Cost Optimization focuses on financial spend, not environmental impact, though the two can be related.
distractorExplanations.c: Security focuses on protecting systems and data.
distractorExplanations.d: Performance Efficiency focuses on matching resources to workload needs for performance, not environmental impact specifically.

questions.hint: This is the sixth and newest pillar.

questions.questionText: A company wants to completely rearchitect a legacy monolithic application into microservices to take full advantage of cloud-native features. Which migration strategy is this?
questions.correctExplanation: Refactoring, or re-architecting, is driven by a strong business need to add features, scale, or performance that would otherwise be difficult in the application's existing environment, typically by moving to a cloud-native architecture such as microservices.

distractorExplanations.b: Rehosting is a lift-and-shift with minimal changes, not a rearchitecture into microservices.
distractorExplanations.c: Repurchasing means moving to a different product, typically a SaaS platform, rather than rebuilding the application's architecture.
distractorExplanations.d: Retaining means keeping the application in its source environment, not migrating or rearchitecting it.

questions.hint: This strategy involves the most significant architectural change.

questions.questionText: Which statement accurately describes an advantage of AWS Cloud's global infrastructure for a company expanding into new international markets?

options.text: The company can deploy applications to AWS Regions closer to end users to reduce latency, without building new physical data centers
The company must build a new data center in every country before using AWS in that Region
AWS requires a separate account for each new country of operation
AWS Regions automatically transfer customer data ownership to AWS

questions.correctExplanation: AWS's global network of Regions and Availability Zones lets customers deploy applications closer to end users in minutes, improving latency and user experience without any physical infrastructure investment.

distractorExplanations.b: This is the opposite of the cloud benefit; no physical data center build-out is required to use a new AWS Region.
distractorExplanations.c: A single AWS account can be used across multiple Regions; a new account per country is not required.
distractorExplanations.d: Customers always retain ownership and control of their content under the AWS Customer Agreement and shared responsibility model.

questions.hint: Think about the 'go global in minutes' benefit.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best describes 'agility' as an AWS Cloud benefit?

options.text: The increased speed and ease with which IT resources can be provisioned, giving businesses the ability to experiment quickly
The pooling of computing resources to serve many customers using a multi-tenant model
The ability to pay only for the resources that are consumed
The removal of the need to manage any operating system patches

questions.correctExplanation: Agility refers to the ease and speed with which cloud resources can be accessed and used, allowing developers to rapidly develop, test, and launch software applications.

distractorExplanations.b: This describes economies of scale / multi-tenancy, a separate benefit from agility.
distractorExplanations.c: This describes the pay-as-you-go pricing model, not agility specifically.
distractorExplanations.d: Patch management responsibility depends on the specific service and the shared responsibility model, and is not the definition of agility.

questions.hint: Consider how quickly new ideas can be tested.

questions.questionText: A company currently spends significant capital purchasing servers that are only used at full capacity a few weeks per year. Which cloud computing benefit most directly addresses this inefficiency?

options.text: Stop guessing capacity by provisioning the amount of resources actually needed
Increase speed and agility of software releases
Benefit from massive economies of scale

questions.correctExplanation: In the cloud, companies can access as much or as little capacity as they need and scale up or down as required, eliminating the need to over-provision hardware for occasional peak demand.

distractorExplanations.b: Speed and agility relates to how quickly resources can be provisioned for development, not fixing over-provisioning of fixed hardware.
distractorExplanations.c: Going global in minutes relates to geographic deployment, not capacity sizing.
distractorExplanations.d: Economies of scale is about AWS's aggregated purchasing power lowering prices, not directly about the customer's own capacity planning problem.

questions.hint: Think about elastic scaling versus fixed hardware purchases.

questions.questionText: Which approach follows the principle of least privilege?

options.text: Grant administrator access to every user
Grant only the permissions required for the task
Share root credentials with the team

questions.correctExplanation: Least privilege limits access to the actions and resources needed for a task, reducing unnecessary authority.

distractorExplanations.a: Administrator access grants permissions beyond the user's task.
distractorExplanations.c: Sharing root credentials exposes broad account privileges and undermines individual accountability.
distractorExplanations.d: Unused permissions retain unnecessary access and should be reviewed and removed.

questions.hint: Consider how much access the task actually requires.

questions.questionText: Which practices improve AWS identity security? Select TWO.

options.text: Embed long-term access keys in application source code
Use IAM roles with temporary credentials for workloads
Use root credentials for routine application requests

questions.correctExplanation: MFA adds another authentication factor for IAM users. Workload roles supply temporary credentials without embedding long-term keys.

distractorExplanations.b: Source code can expose persistent credentials through repositories or distributed copies.
distractorExplanations.d: Root credentials grant excessive privileges for routine application tasks.
distractorExplanations.e: Unused keys retain an avoidable access path and should be removed.

questions.hint: Look for stronger authentication and fewer persistent credentials.

questions.questionText: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, who is responsible for patching the guest operating system on an Amazon EC2 instance?
questions.correctExplanation: For EC2, which is an infrastructure-as-a-service offering, the customer is responsible for 'security in the cloud,' which includes managing the guest operating system, including updates and security patches.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS is responsible for 'security of the cloud' — the underlying hardware, virtualization layer, and facilities — not the guest OS running on customer-managed EC2 instances.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Support provides help but does not take on the customer's operational responsibility for patching the guest OS by default.
distractorExplanations.d: Third-party auditors assess compliance; they are not responsible for operational patching.

questions.hint: EC2 is an IaaS offering where the customer manages the OS.

questions.questionText: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which of the following is always an AWS responsibility, regardless of which services a customer uses?

options.text: Security of the physical facilities that house AWS data centers
Configuring security group rules for an application
Encrypting customer data at the application layer

questions.correctExplanation: AWS is always responsible for 'security of the cloud,' including the physical security of data centers, the hardware, and the global infrastructure, regardless of which services the customer uses.

distractorExplanations.b: Configuring security groups is a customer responsibility, part of 'security in the cloud.'
distractorExplanations.c: Application-layer encryption is generally a customer responsibility.
distractorExplanations.d: Managing IAM users and permissions is always a customer responsibility.

questions.hint: This is part of AWS's 'security of the cloud' responsibility.

questions.questionText: A company needs to centrally manage fine-grained permissions across multiple AWS accounts. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this?

options.text: AWS Organizations with service control policies

questions.correctExplanation: AWS Organizations lets a company centrally manage and govern multiple AWS accounts, and service control policies (SCPs) set permission guardrails across those accounts.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon CloudWatch is a monitoring and observability service, not an account/permissions management tool.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Trusted Advisor provides best-practice recommendations, not centralized multi-account permission management.
distractorExplanations.d: S3 bucket policies control access to a specific bucket, not permissions across multiple accounts.

questions.hint: Think about managing many accounts as a single organization.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service allows a company to store, rotate, and control access to database credentials and API keys, reducing the need to hardcode secrets in application code?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Secrets Manager helps protect secrets such as database credentials and API keys, and can automatically rotate them, removing the need to hardcode sensitive credentials in code.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon Inspector performs automated vulnerability management scans of workloads, not secrets storage.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Shield provides DDoS protection, unrelated to secrets management.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes and compliance, not credential storage.

questions.hint: This service specializes in rotating and storing credentials.

questions.questionText: A security team wants a fully managed service that continuously monitors AWS accounts and workloads for malicious activity using threat intelligence feeds and anomaly detection. Which service should they use?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that continuously monitors for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior using machine learning and integrated threat intelligence.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS Artifact is a self-service portal for accessing AWS compliance reports, not a threat detection service.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS IAM Identity Center provides centralized workforce identity and single sign-on, not threat detection.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon Cognito manages user sign-up, sign-in, and access control for web/mobile apps, not threat monitoring.

questions.hint: Think 'intelligent threat detection'.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides on-demand access to AWS security and compliance reports, such as SOC and PCI reports?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Artifact is a self-service portal that provides on-demand access to AWS compliance reports and select online agreements.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS Trusted Advisor gives recommendations across cost, performance, security, and fault tolerance, but does not host compliance reports.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Config tracks and evaluates resource configurations, not compliance report access.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS CloudTrail records API activity for auditing, not compliance report retrieval.

questions.hint: Think of a document repository for audit reports.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service records a history of API calls made in an AWS account, useful for security analysis, resource change tracking, and compliance auditing?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS CloudTrail records account activity and API usage across AWS infrastructure, providing an event history useful for security analysis, resource tracking, and compliance auditing.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon CloudWatch monitors metrics, logs, and alarms for operational performance, not primarily an API call audit trail.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS X-Ray helps developers analyze and debug distributed applications, not audit API calls.
distractorExplanations.d: The AWS Health Dashboard reports on the health of AWS services and any events affecting an account, not API call history.

questions.hint: Think about an audit trail of 'who did what and when.'

questions.questionText: Which TWO features are core components of an IAM policy that determine whether a request is allowed?

options.text: Resource (the AWS resource the action applies to)
The customer's credit card expiration date

questions.correctExplanation: IAM policies are JSON documents that define which Actions are allowed or denied on which Resources (along with Effect and optional Condition elements).

distractorExplanations.c: Billing address is unrelated to IAM policy evaluation.
distractorExplanations.d: The physical location of an Availability Zone is not a factor in IAM policy evaluation.
distractorExplanations.e: Credit card details are unrelated to permissions evaluation.

questions.hint: IAM policies define who can do what to which resource.

questions.questionText: A company wants to protect its public-facing web application from common Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. Which AWS service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Shield is a managed service that provides protection against Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks for applications running on AWS.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS KMS manages encryption keys, not DDoS protection.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Certificate Manager provisions and manages SSL/TLS certificates, not DDoS protection.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon Macie discovers and protects sensitive data using machine learning, not DDoS mitigation.

questions.hint: Think about attacks that flood a service with traffic.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service uses machine learning to automatically discover, classify, and protect sensitive data such as personally identifiable information (PII) stored in Amazon S3?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and help protect sensitive data, such as PII, stored in Amazon S3.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that filters malicious web traffic, not a data discovery/classification tool.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon Detective helps analyze and visualize security data to investigate potential issues, but is not focused on discovering sensitive data in storage.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Firewall Manager centrally manages firewall rules across accounts, not sensitive data discovery.

questions.hint: This service specializes in finding sensitive data like PII.

questions.questionText: In the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, for a managed service such as Amazon RDS, who is responsible for patching the underlying database engine software?

options.text: A third-party contractor hired by the customer

questions.correctExplanation: For managed services like Amazon RDS, AWS takes on more operational responsibility, including patching the underlying database engine, as part of its 'security of the cloud' and managed-service responsibilities.

distractorExplanations.b: For managed database services, the customer is not responsible for patching the underlying engine; this shifts compared to a self-managed database on EC2.
distractorExplanations.c: There is no requirement or standard practice to hire a third party for this; it's handled by AWS as part of the managed service.
distractorExplanations.d: Patching is not optional; it is necessary for security and is handled by AWS for this managed service.

questions.hint: Managed services shift more operational burden to AWS.

questions.questionText: Which TWO statements correctly describe temporary security credentials issued through AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS)?

options.text: They expire after a defined period of time.
They can be used after expiration if the original role still exists.
They are stored permanently with an IAM user in the same way as long-term access keys.
They include a session token in addition to an access key ID and secret access key.
They are permanent credentials that remain valid until manually deleted.

questions.correctExplanation: AWS STS issues temporary credentials that have a limited lifetime. A temporary credential set contains an access key ID, a secret access key, and a session token, distinguishing it from ordinary long-term access keys.

distractorExplanations.b: After temporary credentials expire, requests signed with that expired credential set are no longer accepted.
distractorExplanations.c: Temporary credentials are generated dynamically for a session rather than stored as permanent user credentials.
distractorExplanations.e: Temporary credentials are short-lived and stop being recognized after they expire.

questions.hint: Temporary credentials are short-lived and have one extra credential component.

questions.questionText: A company must comply with a regulation requiring data to remain within a specific country's borders. Which AWS feature primarily allows the company to control the geographic location where its data is stored?

options.text: Selecting a specific AWS Region for resource deployment

questions.correctExplanation: Customers choose the AWS Region(s) in which to store their content, and AWS does not move or replicate content outside a customer's chosen Region(s) unless the customer configures such replication, supporting data residency requirements.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network that caches content at edge locations globally, which could actually work against strict data residency unless configured carefully.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated network connection to AWS, not control over data storage location.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced DDoS protection, unrelated to data residency.

questions.hint: Think about where you choose to physically deploy resources.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service helps customers manage encryption keys and control how they are used to encrypt data across AWS services?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS KMS makes it easy to create and manage cryptographic keys and control their use across a wide range of AWS services and applications.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS Certificate Manager provisions, manages, and deploys SSL/TLS certificates, not general-purpose encryption key management.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon Cognito handles user identity and access for apps, not encryption key management.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS IAM Identity Center manages workforce single sign-on and centralized access, not encryption keys.

questions.hint: This is AWS's dedicated encryption key management service.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a customer responsibility under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model when using Amazon S3?

options.text: Configuring bucket policies and access permissions
Ensuring the durability of the underlying storage infrastructure

questions.correctExplanation: For Amazon S3, customers are responsible for configuring access controls such as bucket policies, IAM permissions, and encryption settings — this is part of 'security in the cloud.'

distractorExplanations.b: Maintaining physical storage hardware is an AWS responsibility ('security of the cloud').
distractorExplanations.c: Patching the underlying S3 service software is managed entirely by AWS.
distractorExplanations.d: Ensuring durability of the underlying infrastructure is an AWS responsibility, though customers should still follow best practices like versioning.

questions.hint: Think about access configuration versus underlying infrastructure.

questions.questionText: A company needs a centralized place to view and remediate its security posture and compliance status across multiple AWS accounts by aggregating findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, and Macie. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Security Hub provides a comprehensive view of security alerts and security posture across AWS accounts, aggregating and prioritizing findings from services like GuardDuty, Inspector, and Macie.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon Inspector is one of the source services whose findings feed into Security Hub, but it does not itself aggregate findings from other services.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Systems Manager helps manage and operate infrastructure at scale, not aggregate security findings.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance, but is not the central aggregation point for multi-service security findings.

questions.hint: Think about a single-pane-of-glass for security findings.

questions.questionText: Which TWO of the following are examples of AWS compliance programs or certifications that AWS Artifact provides reports and documentation for?

options.text: The customer's own internal HR policy documents

questions.correctExplanation: AWS Artifact provides access to AWS's compliance reports, including SOC reports and PCI DSS compliance documentation, which customers can use for their own audits.

distractorExplanations.c: Internal HR policies are the customer's own documents, unrelated to AWS compliance reports.
distractorExplanations.d: Personal tax records are not part of AWS Artifact's compliance documentation.
distractorExplanations.e: Proprietary customer source code is not something AWS Artifact provides or stores.

questions.hint: Think about industry-recognized third-party audit reports.

questions.questionText: An administrator wants evidence about when an IAM user, role, group, or policy last accessed AWS services so unused permissions can be identified and removed. Which IAM information should the administrator review?

options.text: Service last accessed information in IAM Access Advisor

questions.correctExplanation: IAM provides service last accessed information through Access Advisor. Administrators can use this information to identify permissions that have not been used and refine access toward least privilege.

distractorExplanations.a: EC2 system logs are not the IAM feature that summarizes service last-accessed information for identities and policies.
distractorExplanations.b: Artifact agreements are compliance and contractual resources, not IAM permission-usage data.
distractorExplanations.d: Billing profile information does not show when IAM identities or policies last used AWS services.

questions.hint: Look for IAM evidence that helps remove unused permissions.

questions.questionText: Which AWS compute service lets developers upload code and run it in response to events without provisioning or managing servers?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Lambda is a serverless, event-driven compute service that lets you run code without provisioning or managing servers, automatically scaling based on incoming requests.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon EC2 provides virtual servers that customers must provision, configure, and manage.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Outposts extends AWS infrastructure to on-premises locations, not a serverless code-execution service.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon Lightsail provides simplified virtual private servers, but still involves managing an instance rather than being purely event-driven serverless.

questions.hint: This service runs code without managing any servers.

questions.questionText: Which Amazon EC2 pricing model provides the largest discount in exchange for committing to a consistent amount of usage for a 1- or 3-year term?
questions.correctExplanation: Reserved Instances provide a significant discount (up to 72%) compared to On-Demand pricing in exchange for committing to a specific instance configuration for a 1- or 3-year term.

distractorExplanations.b: On-Demand Instances offer the most flexibility with no commitment but at the highest per-hour rate, not the largest discount.
distractorExplanations.c: Spot Instances can offer even steeper discounts than Reserved Instances but are based on spare capacity and can be interrupted, so they are not a committed-usage discount model.
distractorExplanations.d: Dedicated Hosts billed on-demand do not include the long-term commitment discount that Reserved Instances provide.

questions.hint: Think about committing to usage for a term length.

questions.questionText: Which EC2 pricing option allows a company to use spare AWS compute capacity at steep discounts, but instances can be reclaimed by AWS with short notice?
questions.correctExplanation: Spot Instances let customers use spare EC2 capacity at up to a 90% discount compared to On-Demand prices, but AWS can reclaim the capacity with a two-minute interruption notice.

distractorExplanations.b: On-Demand Instances are billed by the second/hour with no commitment and are not interruptible by AWS in this way.
distractorExplanations.c: Reserved Instances require a 1- or 3-year commitment and are not subject to AWS reclaiming capacity.
distractorExplanations.d: Savings Plans provide discounts for a committed level of usage, not spare-capacity access subject to interruption.

questions.hint: This uses unused capacity and can be interrupted.

questions.questionText: A company wants to run containerized applications without having to manage the underlying EC2 instances themselves. Which option best fits this need?

options.text: Amazon ECS or EKS with AWS Fargate
Amazon EC2 with manually installed Docker

questions.correctExplanation: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers that works with Amazon ECS and EKS, removing the need to provision or manage EC2 instances for running containers.

distractorExplanations.b: Running Docker on manually managed EC2 instances still requires the customer to manage the underlying servers.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Snowball is a physical data transfer device, unrelated to container orchestration.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon WorkSpaces provides virtual desktops, not container hosting.

questions.hint: This option removes server management for containers.

questions.questionText: Which AWS storage service provides object storage designed for 99.999999999% (11 nines) of durability, commonly used for backups, data lakes, and static website hosting?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service) is an object storage service designed for 99.999999999% durability, widely used for backups, data lakes, and static content hosting.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon EBS provides block storage volumes attached to individual EC2 instances, not general-purpose object storage.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon EFS provides scalable file storage for use with EC2, using the NFS protocol, not object storage.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon FSx provides managed file systems (such as Windows File Server or Lustre), not general object storage.

questions.hint: This is AWS's flagship object storage service.

questions.questionText: Which Amazon S3 storage class is best suited for data that is rarely accessed but must be retrieved within milliseconds when needed, at a lower storage cost than S3 Standard?
questions.correctExplanation: S3 Standard-IA is designed for infrequently accessed data that still needs millisecond access when required, at a lower per-GB storage price than S3 Standard, with a retrieval fee.

distractorExplanations.b: S3 Standard is optimized for frequently accessed data and costs more for storage than S3 Standard-IA.
distractorExplanations.c: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is for long-term archival with retrieval times measured in hours, not milliseconds.
distractorExplanations.d: The Archive Access tier within S3 Intelligent-Tiering has retrieval times similar to Glacier, not millisecond access.

questions.hint: Think about infrequent access but fast retrieval.

questions.questionText: Which AWS storage service provides block-level storage volumes for use with Amazon EC2 instances, similar to attaching a hard drive to a server?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon EBS provides persistent block-level storage volumes for use with EC2 instances, functioning like an attached hard drive for the instance's operating system and applications.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon S3 is object storage, accessed via API/HTTP rather than as a mounted block device.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network (CDN), not a block storage service.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises environments to cloud storage, not a direct block storage volume for EC2.

questions.hint: Think of storage that attaches to a virtual server like a hard drive.

questions.questionText: A company needs a fully managed relational database service that supports engines like MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server, without manually managing database server infrastructure. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service supporting multiple engines (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server, and Amazon Aurora), automating tasks like backups and patching.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value/document database, not a relational database service.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon ElastiCache is an in-memory caching service (Redis/Memcached), not a relational database.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon Redshift is a data warehousing service optimized for analytics, not a general-purpose relational OLTP database.

questions.hint: Think of a managed SQL database service supporting multiple engines.

questions.questionText: Which AWS database service is a fully managed, key-value and document NoSQL database that delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL key-value and document database designed to deliver consistent, single-digit millisecond latency at virtually any scale.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon RDS is for relational (SQL) databases, not NoSQL key-value/document data.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse for analytical queries over large datasets, not a low-latency NoSQL store.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon Neptune is a managed graph database, not a key-value/document store.

questions.hint: Think NoSQL, key-value, extremely fast at scale.

questions.questionText: Which AWS networking service lets customers create a logically isolated virtual network within AWS where they can launch resources such as EC2 instances?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) lets customers provision a logically isolated section of the AWS Cloud where they can launch resources in a virtual network they define, including subnets, route tables, and gateways.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon Route 53 is a DNS and domain registration service, not a virtual network construct.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated physical network connection from on-premises to AWS, not a virtual network within AWS.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon CloudFront is a CDN for delivering content, not a virtual network.

questions.hint: Think of your own isolated network inside AWS.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service is a scalable Domain Name System (DNS) web service used for domain registration, DNS routing, and health checking?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon Route 53 is a highly available and scalable DNS web service that can also perform domain registration, DNS routing, and health checks.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon VPC provides virtual networking within AWS, not DNS or domain registration services.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Global Accelerator improves availability and performance by routing traffic through the AWS global network, but it is not primarily a DNS/domain registration service.
distractorExplanations.d: Elastic Load Balancing distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets, not DNS management.

questions.hint: Think about resolving domain names to IP addresses.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service automatically distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets, such as EC2 instances, to improve availability and fault tolerance?
questions.correctExplanation: Elastic Load Balancing automatically distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets, such as EC2 instances, containers, and IP addresses, improving fault tolerance and availability.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling adjusts the number of EC2 instances automatically based on demand, but does not itself distribute incoming traffic across targets.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon Route 53 can route DNS traffic in various ways but is not the primary application-layer load balancing service.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Transit Gateway connects VPCs and on-premises networks through a central hub, not application traffic load balancing.

questions.hint: Think about spreading traffic across multiple servers.

questions.questionText: A company wants its EC2 fleet to automatically add or remove instances based on real-time demand to maintain application availability while controlling cost. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling helps maintain application availability by automatically adding or removing EC2 instances according to defined scaling policies, conditions, and health checks.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS Batch is designed for running batch computing jobs at scale, not general web application traffic-based scaling.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon Lightsail is a simplified VPS offering aimed at simple workloads and does not provide the same fine-grained auto scaling capabilities.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is an orchestration service for deploying applications and uses EC2 Auto Scaling under the hood; it is not itself the scaling mechanism.

questions.hint: Think about dynamically adjusting the number of running instances.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides a global content delivery network (CDN) that caches content at edge locations to reduce latency for end users?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network service that securely delivers data, videos, and applications with low latency by caching content at edge locations close to end users.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated network connection from on-premises to AWS, not content caching at edge locations.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon VPC is a virtual networking service, not a content delivery network.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Transit Gateway connects multiple VPCs and on-premises networks, not a CDN.

questions.hint: Think about edge caching for faster content delivery.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides a dedicated, private network connection between a customer's data center and AWS, bypassing the public internet?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated, private, physical network connection between an on-premises data center and AWS, providing more consistent network performance than internet-based connections.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS Site-to-Site VPN creates an encrypted connection over the public internet, not a dedicated private physical link.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon Route 53 provides DNS services, not dedicated network connectivity.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon API Gateway is for creating and managing APIs, unrelated to private network connectivity to a data center.

questions.hint: This bypasses the public internet with a dedicated physical link.

questions.questionText: What is the relationship between AWS Regions and Availability Zones?

options.text: A Region is a geographic area that contains multiple, isolated Availability Zones connected by low-latency links
An Availability Zone contains multiple Regions
Regions and Availability Zones are the same thing, just different names
A Region is a single physical data center

questions.correctExplanation: An AWS Region is a physical geographic location containing multiple, isolated Availability Zones (each one or more discrete data centers), which are connected through high-bandwidth, low-latency networking.

distractorExplanations.b: This reverses the relationship; Regions contain Availability Zones, not the other way around.
distractorExplanations.c: Regions and Availability Zones are distinct concepts at different levels of the infrastructure hierarchy.
distractorExplanations.d: A Region is a broader geographic area comprising multiple Availability Zones, not a single data center.

questions.hint: Think hierarchy: geography > isolated zones.

questions.questionText: A company wants to design a highly available architecture that can withstand the failure of an entire data center. What should it do?

options.text: Deploy resources across multiple Availability Zones within a Region
Deploy all resources in a single Availability Zone for simplicity
Use only one EC2 instance with no redundancy
Rely solely on daily manual backups stored on the same instance

questions.correctExplanation: Deploying across multiple Availability Zones, which are physically separate data centers within a Region, provides resilience against the failure of any single data center or facility.

distractorExplanations.b: Deploying in a single Availability Zone leaves the application vulnerable if that data center experiences an outage.
distractorExplanations.c: A single instance with no redundancy provides no fault tolerance at all.
distractorExplanations.d: Manual backups on the same instance would be lost along with the instance in a failure and don't provide high availability.

questions.hint: Think about spreading resources across isolated data centers.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides a managed message queuing service that decouples the components of a distributed application?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon SQS is a fully managed message queuing service that lets you decouple and scale microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications by passing messages through queues.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon SNS is a publish/subscribe messaging and notification service, distributing messages to multiple subscribers rather than queuing for point-to-point processing.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Step Functions orchestrates workflows across multiple services using state machines, not simple message queuing.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon EventBridge is a serverless event bus for connecting applications using events, distinct from a traditional message queue.

questions.hint: Think about a queue that holds messages between application components.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service is a fully managed publish/subscribe messaging service used to fan out notifications to multiple subscribers, such as email, SMS, or Lambda functions?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon SNS is a fully managed pub/sub messaging service that can fan out messages to a large number of subscribers, including email, SMS, mobile push, and Lambda functions.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon SQS is a point-to-point message queuing service, not a pub/sub fan-out notification service.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon SES is specifically for sending and receiving email, not general multi-protocol pub/sub notifications.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS AppSync is a managed GraphQL and Pub/Sub API service for application data, a different use case from general fan-out notifications.

questions.hint: Think about publish/subscribe fan-out notifications.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service allows developers to build and train machine learning models without needing deep expertise in the underlying ML infrastructure?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon SageMaker is a fully managed service that provides tools to build, train, and deploy machine learning models at scale, abstracting away much of the underlying infrastructure complexity.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon Comprehend is a natural language processing service for extracting insights from text, a pre-built AI service rather than a general model-building platform.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon Kendra is an intelligent search service, not a general ML model-building platform.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon Textract extracts text and data from scanned documents, a specific pre-built AI service rather than a general-purpose ML platform.

questions.hint: This is AWS's flagship end-to-end ML platform.

questions.questionText: A retail company wants to add product recommendation capabilities to its e-commerce site using the same technology Amazon.com uses, without building a custom ML model from scratch. Which AWS service is designed for this?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon Personalize is a machine learning service that enables developers to build applications with real-time personalized recommendations, based on the same technology used by Amazon.com.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon Rekognition provides image and video analysis, not product recommendations.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon Polly converts text into lifelike speech, unrelated to recommendation engines.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text, unrelated to product recommendations.

questions.hint: Think about a managed recommendation engine service.

questions.questionText: Which TWO statements describe Amazon DocumentDB?

options.text: It is a managed document database service designed for document-oriented workloads.
It is an in-memory caching service compatible with Redis or Memcached.
It is AWS's managed graph database service.
It supports MongoDB-compatible APIs for many applications and tools.
It is a relational database engine that requires tables joined with SQL.

questions.correctExplanation: Amazon DocumentDB is a fully managed document database service designed for JSON-like document workloads and provides MongoDB-compatible APIs, helping many MongoDB-oriented applications and tools work with the service.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon ElastiCache provides managed in-memory caching; DocumentDB is persistent document database storage.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon Neptune is the AWS managed graph database service.
distractorExplanations.e: Amazon DocumentDB is a non-relational document database rather than a general relational SQL engine.

questions.hint: Think managed document data and MongoDB compatibility.

questions.questionText: Which service provides a fully managed data warehouse optimized for running complex analytical queries across large volumes of structured data?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon Redshift is a fully managed, petabyte-scale data warehouse service optimized for running complex analytic queries against large datasets using columnar storage.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon RDS is optimized for transactional (OLTP) relational workloads, not large-scale analytical queries.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database optimized for low-latency key-value access, not complex analytical joins.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon ElastiCache is an in-memory caching service, not a data warehouse.

questions.hint: Think 'data warehouse for analytics'.

questions.questionText: Which deployment/management tool allows developers to describe AWS infrastructure using code (templates) so it can be provisioned consistently and repeatably?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS CloudFormation lets you model, provision, and manage AWS resources by treating infrastructure as code using templates, enabling consistent and repeatable deployments.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon CloudWatch monitors resources and applications, it does not provision infrastructure.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Config tracks resource configuration and compliance over time, but does not provision resources from templates.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Trusted Advisor provides best-practice recommendations, not infrastructure-as-code provisioning.

questions.hint: Think 'Infrastructure as Code'.

questions.questionText: A development team wants to deploy a web application and have AWS automatically handle capacity provisioning, load balancing, and health monitoring, while the team retains full control of the underlying resources if needed. Which service fits best?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is an orchestration service that automatically handles deployment details like capacity provisioning, load balancing, and health monitoring, while still giving developers access to the underlying AWS resources.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS Lambda is for running discrete functions in response to events, not a full application deployment/orchestration platform with retained infrastructure access.
distractorExplanations.c: S3 static website hosting only serves static content and cannot run a full dynamic web application with backend logic.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Snowmobile is an exabyte-scale physical data transfer service, unrelated to application deployment.

questions.hint: This service orchestrates deployment while giving access to underlying resources.

questions.questionText: A company wants an AWS-native, fully managed container orchestration service for deploying and managing containerized applications without requiring a Kubernetes control plane. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon ECS is AWS's fully managed, AWS-native container orchestration service. It schedules and manages containers without requiring customers to operate a Kubernetes control plane.

distractorExplanations.a: Amazon ECR stores and manages container images but does not orchestrate running containers.
distractorExplanations.b: Amazon EKS is the AWS managed Kubernetes service; the scenario specifically does not require Kubernetes.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS CodeBuild compiles, tests, and packages source code; it is not a container orchestration service.

questions.hint: Choose the AWS-native orchestrator rather than Kubernetes.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service provides real-time monitoring of AWS resources and applications, including metrics, logs, dashboards, and alarms?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon CloudWatch collects and tracks metrics, collects and monitors log files, and sets alarms, giving a real-time view of resource and application performance.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS CloudTrail focuses on logging API activity for governance and auditing, not general performance metrics/dashboards.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Config tracks configuration changes and compliance over time, not real-time performance metrics.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS X-Ray helps trace and debug distributed application requests, a narrower focus than CloudWatch's broad monitoring.

questions.hint: Think metrics, dashboards, and alarms.

questions.questionText: A media company needs to transfer 200 TB of video archives from an on-premises data center to AWS but has limited internet bandwidth. Which AWS service is best suited to physically ship this data to AWS?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Snowball is a physical data transport device used to securely transfer large amounts of data into and out of AWS, ideal for large datasets where network transfer would be too slow.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated network link, but still requires sufficient network bandwidth and setup time, unlike physically shipping a device.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds up transfers over the internet using CloudFront edge locations, but is still bound by available internet bandwidth.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Site-to-Site VPN provides an encrypted network connection over the internet, not a physical shipping solution for bandwidth-constrained transfers.

questions.hint: Think about physically shipping a device loaded with data.

questions.questionText: Which AWS service allows customers to create, publish, maintain, and secure APIs at scale for backend services?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon API Gateway is a fully managed service that makes it easy for developers to create, publish, maintain, monitor, and secure APIs at any scale.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS AppConfig helps manage application configuration and feature flags, not API creation and management.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Cloud Map is a service discovery tool for cloud resources, not an API management gateway.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS App Runner is a service for quickly deploying containerized web applications, not primarily an API management service.

questions.hint: This service manages the lifecycle of APIs.

questions.questionText: A company wants a fully managed service to run large-scale Apache Spark and Hadoop big data processing jobs without manually configuring clusters. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon EMR (Elastic MapReduce) is a managed big data platform that simplifies running large-scale distributed data processing frameworks such as Apache Spark and Hadoop.

distractorExplanations.b: Amazon Athena is a serverless interactive query service for analyzing data directly in S3 using SQL, not a Spark/Hadoop cluster management service.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon QuickSight is a business intelligence and data visualization service, not a big data processing framework.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Glue DataBrew is a visual data preparation tool, not a general Spark/Hadoop cluster management platform.

questions.hint: Think managed Hadoop/Spark clusters.

questions.questionText: Which TWO are managed file system offerings available through Amazon FSx?

options.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

questions.correctExplanation: Amazon FSx provides managed file systems for specialized workloads, including Amazon FSx for Windows File Server and Amazon FSx for Lustre. These provide file-system semantics rather than object, block, or database storage.

distractorExplanations.a: Amazon EBS gp3 is block storage for EC2, not an Amazon FSx file system.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon S3 is object storage, not an Amazon FSx managed file system.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL database, not a file system.

questions.hint: Think Windows SMB and high-performance Lustre file systems.

questions.questionText: Which AWS tool allows customers to create budgets that alert them when their AWS costs or usage exceed (or are forecasted to exceed) a defined threshold?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Budgets lets customers set custom cost and usage budgets and receive alerts when actual or forecasted spend exceeds the budgeted amount.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes historical and forecasted spending patterns but does not itself create threshold-based alerts the way Budgets does.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Pricing Calculator estimates the cost of AWS services before they are used, not after-the-fact spend alerting.
distractorExplanations.d: The AWS Cost and Usage Report provides detailed billing data for analysis, but does not proactively send threshold alerts on its own.

questions.hint: This tool sends alerts when spending crosses a threshold.

questions.questionText: Which AWS tool lets a prospective customer estimate the cost of a proposed AWS architecture before deploying any resources?
questions.correctExplanation: The AWS Pricing Calculator lets users build out a hypothetical architecture and estimate the cost of AWS services before actually provisioning any resources.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS Cost Explorer analyzes actual historical and forecasted spend from resources already in use, not hypothetical pre-deployment estimates.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Budgets tracks and alerts on actual spend against a budget, not pre-deployment cost estimation.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Trusted Advisor provides recommendations on existing resources across several categories, not upfront cost estimation for a new architecture.

questions.hint: Think about estimating cost before deploying anything.

questions.questionText: A company uses multiple AWS accounts for different departments and wants to receive one combined invoice while also benefiting from volume pricing discounts across all accounts. Which feature should it use?

options.text: Individual billing per account with no linkage

questions.correctExplanation: Consolidated billing, a feature of AWS Organizations, combines usage from all member accounts to share volume pricing discounts and Reserved Instance benefits, while providing one bill for the entire organization.

distractorExplanations.b: Billing each account separately would prevent the company from benefiting from combined volume discounts.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Budgets tracks and alerts on spending but does not combine invoices or apply volume discounts across accounts.
distractorExplanations.d: Amazon QuickSight is a business intelligence tool for visualizing data, not a billing consolidation feature.

questions.hint: Think about combining multiple accounts under one bill.

questions.questionText: Which AWS Support plan is the minimum tier that provides access to a Technical Account Manager (TAM)?
questions.correctExplanation: A Technical Account Manager (TAM) is provided as part of the Enterprise and Enterprise On-Ramp Support plans, offering proactive guidance and advocacy.

distractorExplanations.b: The Basic Support plan includes only customer service and access to documentation, forums, and basic checks — no TAM.
distractorExplanations.c: The Developer Support plan provides business-hours email access to Cloud Support Associates, but no TAM.
distractorExplanations.d: The Business Support plan provides 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers, but does not include a dedicated TAM.

questions.hint: This is a dedicated advocate available only at the highest support tiers.

questions.questionText: Which AWS Support plan is designed for customers running production workloads and provides 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers via phone, chat, and email with a response time as fast as under 1 hour for urgent issues?
questions.correctExplanation: Business Support provides 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers via phone, chat, and email, with a response time as fast as under 1 hour for production-system-down cases, suitable for customers running production workloads.

distractorExplanations.b: Basic Support only includes customer service, documentation, whitepapers, and support forums — no direct technical support via phone/chat.
distractorExplanations.c: Developer Support offers business-hours email access with response times up to 24 hours, not 24/7 phone/chat with sub-1-hour urgent response.
distractorExplanations.d: The AWS Free Tier is a pricing offer for limited free usage of services, not a technical support plan.

questions.hint: This plan targets production workloads with fast response times.

questions.questionText: Which AWS tool provides real-time guidance across five categories — cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, and service limits — by comparing account usage against AWS best practices?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Trusted Advisor inspects a customer's AWS environment and provides real-time recommendations across cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, and service limits, based on AWS best practices.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS Cost Explorer focuses specifically on cost and usage analysis and forecasting, not the full set of five Trusted Advisor categories.
distractorExplanations.c: The AWS Health Dashboard reports on the health of AWS services and account-specific events, not best-practice recommendations across those five categories.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Compute Optimizer provides resource-sizing recommendations specifically for compute resources, a narrower scope than Trusted Advisor's five categories.

questions.hint: Think about a tool that checks against best practices in five specific categories.

questions.questionText: A new AWS customer chooses the Free account plan under the current AWS Free Tier. Which statement best describes this plan?

options.text: Every AWS service is free for the first 12 months with no usage limits.

The customer can use Free Tier credits to experiment for up to six months or until the credits are exhausted, whichever occurs first, without incurring charges unless the account is upgraded to a Paid plan.
The Free account plan never expires as long as the customer stays below monthly service limits.
The customer must begin paying standard service charges immediately after creating the account.

questions.correctExplanation: Under the current AWS Free Tier, new customers can choose a Free account plan, receive Free Tier credits, and experiment without charges for up to six months or until the credits are depleted, whichever comes first. A customer can upgrade to a Paid plan to continue using AWS beyond the Free plan limits.

distractorExplanations.a: The current AWS Free Tier does not make every service free for 12 months and still applies service eligibility and usage rules.
distractorExplanations.c: The Free account plan is time- and credit-limited; it does not continue indefinitely.
distractorExplanations.d: The Free account plan uses Free Tier credits and does not incur charges while the account remains on that plan; paid usage begins after upgrading to a Paid plan.

questions.hint: Focus on the current credit-based Free account plan rather than the older 12-month-only model.

questions.questionText: A finance team needs a detailed, line-item breakdown of AWS charges, including usage type and cost allocation tags, for import into their own analytics tools. Which AWS billing feature should they use?
questions.correctExplanation: The AWS Cost and Usage Report provides the most comprehensive set of cost and usage data available, including granular line items and cost allocation tags, suitable for detailed analysis or import into external tools.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS Budgets is used to set spending thresholds and alerts, not to generate detailed line-item billing exports.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Trusted Advisor provides best-practice recommendations, not detailed billing data exports.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Marketplace is a digital catalog for finding and purchasing third-party software, unrelated to billing data exports.

questions.hint: Think about the most granular billing data export available.

questions.questionText: Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets while delivering business value through risk assessments and mitigation strategies?
questions.correctExplanation: The Security pillar focuses on protecting data, systems, and assets and on managing security risk while workloads deliver business value.

distractorExplanations.b: Reliability focuses on consistent operation and recovery from failures, not primarily on protecting information and assets.
distractorExplanations.c: Operational Excellence focuses on running, monitoring, and continually improving systems and processes.
distractorExplanations.d: Sustainability focuses on reducing the environmental impact of cloud workloads.

questions.hint: Think about protection of data, systems, and assets.

questions.questionText: Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar focuses on delivering business value at the lowest price point while avoiding unnecessary costs?
questions.correctExplanation: The Cost Optimization pillar focuses on running systems that deliver business value at the lowest price point and on eliminating unnecessary spending.

distractorExplanations.b: Performance Efficiency focuses on efficient use of computing resources to meet requirements, rather than financial optimization itself.
distractorExplanations.c: Reliability focuses on consistent operation, resilience, and recovery from disruptions.
distractorExplanations.d: Security focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets.

questions.hint: This pillar is about avoiding unnecessary spend.

questions.questionText: A company wants an application to remain accessible even when an individual component fails. Which cloud design objective most directly describes this requirement?
questions.correctExplanation: High availability is the objective of keeping a system available for use despite component failures, typically through redundancy and fault-isolated design.

distractorExplanations.b: Elasticity is the ability to add or remove capacity as demand changes; it does not by itself guarantee availability during failures.
distractorExplanations.c: Durability concerns preserving data over time rather than keeping an application endpoint continuously accessible.
distractorExplanations.d: Agility concerns how quickly resources and solutions can be provisioned and changed.

questions.hint: Focus on minimizing application downtime.

questions.questionText: What is the primary purpose of an AWS Well-Architected Framework review?

options.text: To identify architectural risks and improvement opportunities through a structured review
To certify that a workload is guaranteed to have no outages
To replace all application testing with an AWS audit
To calculate the exact monthly AWS bill

questions.correctExplanation: A Well-Architected review is a structured conversation used to evaluate a workload against AWS architectural best practices, identify risks, and prioritize improvements.

distractorExplanations.b: A review does not certify zero outages or provide an availability guarantee.
distractorExplanations.c: The review is not a replacement for functional, security, or performance testing and is not intended as an audit.
distractorExplanations.d: Cost can be discussed, but the review is broader than producing an exact monthly bill.

questions.hint: It is a best-practice assessment, not a certification.

questions.questionText: Which TWO business outcomes are identified by the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework in addition to reduced business risk and increased operational efficiency?

options.text: Improved environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance
Guaranteed elimination of all technology spending
Automatic removal of every regulatory obligation

questions.correctExplanation: AWS CAF identifies improved ESG performance and increased revenue as key cloud-transformation business outcomes, alongside reduced business risk and increased operational efficiency.

distractorExplanations.c: AWS CAF describes business outcomes that cloud transformation can accelerate; it does not guarantee zero technology spending.
distractorExplanations.d: Using AWS does not remove a customer's regulatory and compliance obligations.
distractorExplanations.e: AWS CAF is specifically about enabling and managing organizational transformation rather than eliminating the need for change.

questions.hint: Think about the four business outcomes in the AWS CAF transformation value chain.

questions.questionText: In the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework, which perspective helps ensure that cloud investments accelerate digital transformation ambitions and business outcomes?
questions.correctExplanation: The Business perspective helps ensure cloud investments support digital transformation ambitions and measurable business outcomes.

distractorExplanations.b: The Platform perspective focuses on building a scalable hybrid cloud platform and modernizing workloads.
distractorExplanations.c: The Security perspective focuses on confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data and cloud workloads.
distractorExplanations.d: The Operations perspective focuses on delivering cloud services at the level agreed with business stakeholders.

questions.hint: Think about linking cloud investment to business outcomes.

questions.questionText: In the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework, which perspective focuses on culture, organizational structure, leadership, and workforce skills needed for cloud transformation?
questions.correctExplanation: The People perspective helps organizations evolve culture, structure, leadership, and workforce capabilities so employees can support cloud transformation.

distractorExplanations.b: Governance focuses on orchestrating cloud initiatives while maximizing benefits and minimizing transformation-related risks.
distractorExplanations.c: Platform focuses on the cloud technology foundation and workload modernization.
distractorExplanations.d: Operations focuses on operating cloud services and meeting business service expectations.

questions.hint: This perspective centers on people and organizational change.

questions.questionText: In the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework, which perspective helps orchestrate cloud initiatives while maximizing organizational benefits and minimizing transformation-related risks?
questions.correctExplanation: The Governance perspective helps coordinate cloud initiatives, establish accountability, maximize benefits, and minimize transformation-related risks.

distractorExplanations.b: Business aligns cloud investment to transformation ambitions and business outcomes.
distractorExplanations.c: People focuses on culture, leadership, organizational structure, and workforce skills.
distractorExplanations.d: Platform focuses on building and modernizing the cloud technology foundation.

questions.hint: Think about oversight, accountability, benefits, and risk.

questions.questionText: In the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework, which perspective focuses on building an enterprise-grade, scalable hybrid cloud platform and modernizing workloads?
questions.correctExplanation: The Platform perspective focuses on building a scalable cloud foundation, modernizing existing workloads, and implementing new cloud-native solutions.

distractorExplanations.b: Security focuses on confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data and workloads.
distractorExplanations.c: Business connects cloud investments to business outcomes.
distractorExplanations.d: People focuses on culture, skills, leadership, and organizational change.

questions.hint: This perspective is closest to the technical cloud foundation.

questions.questionText: In the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework, which perspective focuses on achieving confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data and cloud workloads?
questions.correctExplanation: The Security perspective helps achieve confidentiality, integrity, and availability for data and cloud workloads through security capabilities and controls.

distractorExplanations.b: Operations focuses on operating cloud services according to business requirements.
distractorExplanations.c: Business focuses on business value and transformation outcomes.
distractorExplanations.d: Governance coordinates initiatives, accountability, benefits, and transformation risk.

questions.hint: Think of the CIA security objectives.

questions.questionText: In the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework, which perspective focuses on delivering cloud services at a level agreed with business stakeholders?
questions.correctExplanation: The Operations perspective focuses on ensuring cloud services are delivered and operated at a level that meets the needs agreed with business stakeholders.

distractorExplanations.b: People focuses on culture, organizational structure, leadership, and skills.
distractorExplanations.c: Platform focuses on the technical cloud foundation and workload modernization.
distractorExplanations.d: Governance focuses on orchestrating cloud initiatives and managing transformation risk.

questions.hint: This perspective is about operating services effectively.

questions.questionText: Which TWO are transformation domains identified by the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS CAF describes Technology and Process as two of four transformation domains; the other two are Organization and Product.

distractorExplanations.c: Reliability is a Well-Architected pillar, not one of the four CAF transformation domains.
distractorExplanations.d: An Availability Zone is part of AWS global infrastructure, not a transformation domain.
distractorExplanations.e: Cost Optimization is a Well-Architected pillar, not a CAF transformation domain.

questions.hint: CAF transformation domains describe what an organization transforms.

questions.questionText: Which TWO are business outcomes that AWS CAF says cloud-enabled transformation can help accelerate?

options.text: Remove the need for organizational change
