distractorExplanations.b: AWS Artifact provides AWS compliance reports and agreements rather than commercial software listings.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS Organizations provides multi-account governance and consolidated management, not a third-party software catalog.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS Budgets tracks costs and usage against thresholds but does not sell or deploy software products.

questions.hint: Think AWS's third-party digital catalog.

questions.questionText: Which TWO practices align with the AWS Well-Architected general design principle of testing systems at production scale?

options.text: Purchase permanent duplicate production hardware solely so it is always available for testing.
Decommission the temporary test resources after testing is complete.
Avoid production-scale testing because it can never be economical in the cloud.
Test only individual code functions and avoid exercising the full architecture.
Create a production-scale test environment on demand when it is needed.

questions.correctExplanation: The AWS Well-Architected Framework recommends creating a production-scale test environment on demand, completing the testing, and then decommissioning those resources. This enables realistic validation without the cost of maintaining permanent duplicate infrastructure.

distractorExplanations.a: The cloud allows production-scale test resources to be created on demand, so permanent duplicate hardware is not required for this design principle.
distractorExplanations.c: On-demand cloud resources make production-scale testing practical without permanently owning the test infrastructure.
distractorExplanations.d: Production-scale testing is intended to validate the behavior of the architecture under realistic conditions, not to restrict testing to isolated functions.

questions.hint: Use the cloud's on-demand nature for realistic testing.

questions.questionText: Which AWS Well-Architected general design principle encourages teams to use automation so they can cheaply create, replicate, compare, and revert architectural experiments?

options.text: Automate with architectural experimentation in mind
Freeze the architecture after the first production release
Prefer manual infrastructure changes so each change is unique
Scale every component to its maximum size before testing

questions.correctExplanation: Automation makes architectural experiments repeatable and inexpensive, allows changes to be tracked, and makes it easier to revert to earlier configurations.

distractorExplanations.b: Cloud architecture should be able to evolve; freezing it prevents learning from experiments and changing requirements.
distractorExplanations.c: Manual changes increase inconsistency and make experiments harder to reproduce or reverse.
distractorExplanations.d: Maximum sizing is not the principle; the focus is repeatable experimentation through automation.

questions.hint: Look for the principle that treats infrastructure changes as repeatable experiments.

questions.questionText: A company expects its products and requirements to change frequently. Which Well-Architected general design principle says its systems should be able to change over time rather than depend on one-time architectural decisions?

options.text: Use fixed architectures to eliminate future design decisions
Avoid automation because it can change infrastructure too quickly
Move every workload to the same AWS service

questions.correctExplanation: Evolutionary architectures use the cloud's automation and on-demand testing capabilities to lower the risk of design changes and let systems evolve with business needs.

distractorExplanations.a: Static architecture can become a constraint as business requirements and technology evolve.
distractorExplanations.b: Automation reduces the risk and effort of safely testing and evolving architecture.
distractorExplanations.d: Evolutionary architecture does not require a single service; it allows designs to change as evidence and needs change.

questions.hint: Think about architecture that is expected to evolve instead of remain static.

questions.questionText: An architecture team collects workload telemetry and uses the results to decide whether to change instance families and storage choices. Which Well-Architected general design principle does this demonstrate?

options.text: Avoid measuring production behavior to reduce monitoring cost
Make architectural decisions only from vendor defaults
Use the same architecture for every workload regardless of behavior

questions.correctExplanation: The principle 'drive architectures using data' means measuring how architectural choices affect workload behavior and using that evidence to guide improvements.

distractorExplanations.a: Without measurements, the team cannot make evidence-based architecture improvements.
distractorExplanations.c: The principle calls for fact-based decisions using workload data, not relying only on defaults.
distractorExplanations.d: Different workload data can justify different architectural choices; uniformity is not the goal.

questions.hint: Which principle replaces assumptions with measured evidence?

questions.questionText: A company regularly simulates realistic operational incidents so teams can practice response procedures and discover weaknesses before real failures occur. Which Well-Architected general design principle is this?

options.text: Avoid testing failure scenarios in production-like environments
Treat each incident as an isolated event and do not share lessons
Only review architecture when a customer reports an outage

questions.correctExplanation: Game days deliberately simulate operational events so teams can test architecture and processes, identify weaknesses, and build experience handling failures.

distractorExplanations.b: Game days intentionally simulate events so teams can learn how systems and procedures behave.
distractorExplanations.c: The purpose of game days includes organizational learning and identifying improvements.
distractorExplanations.d: Game days are proactive exercises, not only reactive reviews after customer-impacting incidents.

questions.hint: Think of scheduled exercises that simulate incidents.

questions.questionText: Under the Operational Excellence pillar, which design principle emphasizes aligning team structures, operating models, goals, and KPIs with the business results the organization is trying to achieve?

options.text: Centralize every operational decision in one approval board
Organize teams only by the AWS services they operate
Measure success only by the number of infrastructure changes completed

questions.correctExplanation: Operational Excellence recommends organizing teams and operating models around measurable business outcomes so operational goals and KPIs support the organization's long-term objectives.

distractorExplanations.a: Excessive centralization can reduce agility and does not define the business-outcome operating model principle.
distractorExplanations.b: Service-based silos do not necessarily align ownership, goals, and KPIs to business outcomes.
distractorExplanations.d: Operational activity is not the same as achieving business outcomes.

questions.hint: Focus on the relationship between operations and business results.

questions.questionText: An operations team combines logs, metrics, traces, and business KPIs so it can understand workload health and act before business outcomes are affected. Which Operational Excellence design principle is this?

options.text: Use manual user reports as the primary health signal
Collect telemetry only for compliance archiving
Disable metrics after the system reaches steady state

questions.correctExplanation: Observability for actionable insights means gaining a comprehensive view of workload behavior and business KPIs and using telemetry to make informed, timely operational decisions.

distractorExplanations.a: Observability relies on workload telemetry and KPIs, not only on users reporting problems.
distractorExplanations.b: Archiving alone does not provide the actionable understanding and timely response described by observability.
distractorExplanations.d: Continuous visibility is needed because workload behavior and risks change over time.

questions.hint: Think beyond simple logging: the goal is actionable understanding.

questions.questionText: Which Operational Excellence principle recommends automating operations while adding safeguards such as approvals, rate controls, and error thresholds to limit the risk of automation?

options.text: Perform repetitive changes manually to preserve control

questions.correctExplanation: Safely automating operations reduces manual error and operator toil while using guardrails such as approvals, thresholds, and rate controls to prevent automation from causing excessive impact.

distractorExplanations.a: Event-driven automation is one of the ways cloud operations can respond consistently and quickly.
distractorExplanations.b: Manual repetitive work increases operator toil and human error and is contrary to the automation principle.
distractorExplanations.c: Unbounded automation can amplify mistakes; the principle explicitly includes safety mechanisms.

questions.hint: Automation is useful, but the key word is safe.

questions.questionText: A deployment strategy releases small changes that can be rolled back quickly instead of making large, infrequent releases. Which Operational Excellence design principle does this follow?

options.text: Prevent components from being updated independently
Make production changes that cannot be rolled back
Batch as many changes as possible into rare releases

questions.correctExplanation: Frequent, small, reversible changes reduce blast radius, make failures easier to recover from, and allow teams to deliver improvements with lower operational risk.

distractorExplanations.b: Loosely coupled components help enable small, isolated, reversible updates.
distractorExplanations.c: Reversibility is a core part of the principle because it reduces the impact of unsuccessful changes.
distractorExplanations.d: Large batches increase blast radius and make failures harder to isolate or reverse.

questions.hint: Smaller changes reduce blast radius.

questions.questionText: An organization reviews its runbooks after using them, updates steps that were unclear, and regularly validates that teams know the procedures. Which Operational Excellence principle is being applied?

options.text: Review procedures only after a major outage
Keep procedures unchanged so every incident is handled identically forever
Replace written procedures with tribal knowledge

questions.correctExplanation: Operational procedures should be reviewed, practiced, and improved as workloads evolve and teams learn, with updates communicated to relevant stakeholders.

distractorExplanations.a: The principle calls for frequent refinement and regular validation, not only post-outage review.
distractorExplanations.c: Procedures should evolve as workloads and lessons change; permanently freezing them allows known gaps to persist.
distractorExplanations.d: Relying on undocumented knowledge makes operations less consistent and harder to scale.

questions.hint: Runbooks should evolve with the workload.

questions.questionText: Before a major launch, a team performs pre-mortem exercises, identifies likely failure modes, and tests whether its response procedures work. Which Operational Excellence principle does this demonstrate?

options.text: Wait for incidents to reveal unknown risks
Assume managed services eliminate all failure scenarios

questions.correctExplanation: Anticipating failure means proactively exploring failure scenarios, understanding their business impact, and testing both technical and human response procedures.

distractorExplanations.b: Anticipating failure requires examining and testing failure scenarios, not only normal operation.
distractorExplanations.c: The principle is proactive: identify and test failure scenarios before they occur in real operations.
distractorExplanations.d: Managed services reduce some operational burden but do not remove the need to prepare for workload failures.

questions.hint: Think proactively about failure before the launch.

questions.questionText: After an incident, several teams review metrics and events, document what happened, and share the lessons so other workloads can improve. Which Operational Excellence principle is this?

options.text: Discard telemetry after the incident is resolved
Restrict incident lessons to the team that owned the affected service
Focus only on assigning individual blame for the incident
Learn from all operational events and metrics

questions.correctExplanation: Operational Excellence calls for learning from events, failures, and metrics and sharing those lessons broadly so future operations and business outcomes improve.

distractorExplanations.a: Metrics and events are valuable evidence for understanding causes and improving operations.
distractorExplanations.b: The principle promotes sharing learning across teams and the organization.
distractorExplanations.c: The goal is systemic learning and improvement, not merely assigning blame.

questions.hint: Think about turning every event into organizational learning.

questions.questionText: Which TWO benefits support the Operational Excellence design principle of using managed services when they meet a workload's requirements?

options.text: They can reduce the operational burden of maintaining underlying components.
They require customers to manage more underlying infrastructure than self-managed services.
They transfer all customer security and compliance responsibilities to AWS.
They guarantee that no operational procedures or monitoring are needed.
They can let teams focus more effort on business outcomes instead of routine infrastructure operations.

questions.correctExplanation: Using managed services can reduce the operational burden associated with maintaining underlying infrastructure and allows teams to devote more time to differentiated business outcomes. It does not eliminate the customer's remaining operational or security responsibilities.

distractorExplanations.b: The purpose of using an appropriate managed service is generally to offload more undifferentiated infrastructure operation to AWS, not increase it.
distractorExplanations.c: Managed services shift some operational responsibilities to AWS, but customers still retain responsibilities under the shared responsibility model.
distractorExplanations.d: Managed services reduce some operational work but do not eliminate the need for workload operations, monitoring, or governance.

questions.hint: Think undifferentiated heavy lifting.

questions.questionText: A workload monitors business KPIs and automatically starts a remediation workflow when a threshold indicates a failure. Which Reliability design principle does this illustrate?

options.text: Require an operator to manually detect every fault before recovery starts
Treat monitoring as informational only and never trigger actions
Increase capacity permanently after every incident

questions.correctExplanation: Reliability recommends using meaningful indicators to detect failures and trigger automated processes that work around or repair the problem, reducing recovery time.

distractorExplanations.a: Manual-only detection and recovery are slower and do not demonstrate automatic recovery.
distractorExplanations.c: The principle uses monitoring signals to initiate notification and automated recovery actions.
distractorExplanations.d: Automatic recovery is about responding to failure conditions, not permanently overprovisioning.

questions.hint: Monitoring should lead to automated remediation.

questions.questionText: Which TWO practices align with the Reliability design principle of testing recovery procedures?

options.text: Regularly test how the workload fails and recovers under controlled conditions.
Test recovery only after a real production outage occurs.
Keep all recovery testing manual so results cannot be repeated.
Use automation to simulate failures and validate that recovery mechanisms behave as expected.
Assume recovery procedures work if they are documented, without exercising them.

questions.correctExplanation: Reliability improves when teams deliberately test failure and recovery paths rather than assuming they work. Automated failure simulation can make those exercises repeatable and reveal weaknesses before real incidents occur.

distractorExplanations.b: The design principle calls for proactive testing before real incidents so weaknesses can be discovered safely.
distractorExplanations.c: Automation makes recovery testing repeatable and supports consistent validation of failure and recovery behavior.
distractorExplanations.e: Documentation alone does not verify that recovery mechanisms will work during an actual failure.

questions.hint: Prove recovery works before you need it.

questions.questionText: A service is redesigned from one very large processing node into several smaller nodes behind a distribution layer so one node failure has less impact. Which Reliability principle does this follow?

options.text: Consolidate all requests onto one host
Scale horizontally to increase aggregate workload availability
Keep redundant nodes in the same single point of failure
Scale vertically so a single node becomes larger

questions.correctExplanation: Horizontal scaling replaces reliance on one large resource with multiple smaller resources, reducing the impact of any one failure on the overall workload.

distractorExplanations.a: A single host increases the single-failure blast radius.
distractorExplanations.c: Horizontal scaling improves availability when resources are distributed so they do not share the same failure point.
distractorExplanations.d: Vertical scaling increases the importance of one resource and does not reduce the impact of that resource failing.

questions.hint: Many smaller resources can reduce single-resource failure impact.

questions.questionText: An infrastructure team requires all production infrastructure changes to be applied through version-controlled automation so changes can be reviewed and traced. Which Reliability design principle is this?

options.text: Make infrastructure changes only during hardware replacement cycles
Prevent the automation itself from being versioned
Allow untracked manual changes for urgent convenience

questions.correctExplanation: Managing change through automation makes infrastructure modifications repeatable and reviewable, and the automation itself can be tracked and controlled as it evolves.

distractorExplanations.b: Cloud infrastructure can be changed continuously; the principle focuses on controlled automation rather than hardware cycles.
distractorExplanations.c: The automation is also a change artifact and should be tracked and reviewed.
distractorExplanations.d: Untracked manual changes increase configuration drift and reduce the ability to review or reproduce changes.

questions.hint: Think repeatable, tracked infrastructure changes.

questions.questionText: Which TWO outcomes are associated with the Performance Efficiency principle of democratizing advanced technologies?

options.text: Advanced technologies become available only to organizations that can operate specialized infrastructure themselves.
Teams can consume complex technologies as managed services instead of developing deep operational expertise in each technology.
Teams can focus more on product development while AWS handles more of the underlying technology operation.
Customers no longer need to understand their workload's performance requirements.
Every workload must use the newest AWS service even when it does not meet requirements.

questions.correctExplanation: Democratizing advanced technologies means consuming capabilities such as machine learning or specialized databases as services so teams do not have to become experts in operating the underlying technology and can focus on their own products.

distractorExplanations.a: The principle is the opposite: cloud services make advanced technologies more broadly accessible without requiring every organization to operate the underlying systems.
distractorExplanations.d: Managed services reduce operational complexity, but teams still need to understand workload requirements and evaluate service suitability.
distractorExplanations.e: Performance Efficiency emphasizes appropriate technology choices, not automatically adopting the newest service.

questions.hint: Use advanced capabilities without operating all of the machinery.

questions.questionText: Which Performance Efficiency principle reduces the operational burden of running servers by favoring services where infrastructure provisioning and server management are abstracted away?

options.text: Keep idle servers running so capacity is always available
Host every component on manually managed physical servers
Use only the largest virtual machines available

questions.correctExplanation: Serverless architectures remove the need to provision and maintain servers for suitable workloads, reducing operational burden and often aligning cost with actual requests or events.

distractorExplanations.b: Serverless designs can avoid paying for and managing always-on server capacity when the workload does not require it.
distractorExplanations.c: That approach maximizes rather than removes server-management burden.
distractorExplanations.d: Large VMs still require server-oriented capacity and operations and are not serverless.

questions.hint: Which architecture removes server management from the customer?

questions.questionText: A team rapidly benchmarks several instance types and storage configurations, keeps the best-performing option, and discards the rest. Which Performance Efficiency design principle is illustrated?

options.text: Avoid temporary test resources because they cost money
Choose the first configuration and never revisit it
Optimize performance only through theoretical estimates

questions.correctExplanation: Virtual and automatable cloud resources make it practical to test multiple configurations frequently and use measured results to choose better-performing options.

distractorExplanations.a: On-demand resources make short comparative tests practical and inexpensive relative to permanent infrastructure.
distractorExplanations.b: The principle encourages repeated comparison as services and workload needs evolve.
distractorExplanations.c: The principle encourages empirical testing of real cloud configurations.

questions.hint: Cloud resources make comparative testing fast and disposable.

questions.questionText: An architect chooses a database technology based primarily on the application's actual access patterns instead of selecting the same database engine for every workload. Which Performance Efficiency principle does this demonstrate?

options.text: Select services only by their brand familiarity
Ignore how a service is consumed as long as it is managed
Use one database technology for all access patterns

questions.correctExplanation: Mechanical sympathy means understanding how technologies behave and selecting the service or approach that best matches the workload's specific goals and usage patterns.

distractorExplanations.a: Mechanical sympathy requires matching technology behavior to workload goals, not choosing based on familiarity.
distractorExplanations.b: Managed status alone does not guarantee that the service characteristics match the workload.
distractorExplanations.d: Different access patterns can benefit from different technologies; one-size-fits-all selection ignores workload characteristics.

questions.hint: Match the technology to the workload pattern.

questions.questionText: Which Cost Optimization design principle says an organization should deliberately build financial-management skills, processes, ownership, and governance for cloud spending?

options.text: Optimize costs only once during the initial migration
Leave all cost decisions exclusively to individual developers
Measure cloud success only by reducing the monthly bill

questions.correctExplanation: Cloud Financial Management is an organizational capability that combines knowledge, processes, programs, and ownership so cloud spending can be governed and optimized in support of business value.

distractorExplanations.b: Cloud cost management is an ongoing organizational capability rather than a one-time exercise.
distractorExplanations.c: Effective Cloud Financial Management requires organizational capability, governance, and shared financial accountability.
distractorExplanations.d: Cloud Financial Management connects spending to business value, not just absolute cost reduction.

questions.hint: Think FinOps-like organizational capability, not one isolated cost-cutting action.

questions.questionText: A team tracks the business transactions produced by a workload and compares that output with the workload's AWS cost. Which Cost Optimization design principle is being applied?

options.text: Ignore business output when evaluating cost changes
Judge efficiency only by the lowest hourly instance price
Measure only the number of provisioned resources

questions.correctExplanation: Measuring overall efficiency compares the business output delivered by a workload with the cost required to deliver that output, making cost improvements measurable in business terms.

distractorExplanations.a: The principle explicitly relates cost to the business output delivered by the workload.
distractorExplanations.b: A cheaper unit price can still be inefficient if the workload produces less value or wastes resources.
distractorExplanations.d: Resource count does not show the relationship between cost and business output.

questions.hint: Relate cost to business output, not just infrastructure units.

questions.questionText: Which TWO practices best demonstrate the Cost Optimization principle 'analyze and attribute expenditure'?

options.text: Hide detailed cost data from workload owners
Combine all costs into one unallocated total with no ownership information
Assume every workload should receive an equal share of the total bill
Use attributed cost data to help workload owners measure return on investment and identify optimization opportunities
Associate cloud usage and cost with the workload or owner responsible for it

questions.correctExplanation: Analyze and attribute expenditure means identifying who or what generated cloud usage and cost, then giving owners transparent cost information so they can measure ROI and optimize their resources.

distractorExplanations.a: The principle depends on transparent attribution so owners can understand and optimize their spending.
distractorExplanations.b: A single unallocated total prevents accurate attribution to workloads or owners.
distractorExplanations.c: Equal allocation ignores actual usage and does not provide accurate cost attribution.

questions.hint: Cost attribution should create ownership and transparency.

questions.questionText: Which practice best protects the AWS account root user during normal day-to-day administration?

options.text: Share the root password with senior administrators so someone is always available
Use the root user only for tasks that specifically require root credentials
Use the root user for all administrative tasks because it has every permission
Create applications that authenticate with root credentials

questions.correctExplanation: The root user has unrestricted account access, so AWS recommends using it only for the small set of tasks that require root credentials and using other identities for routine administration.

distractorExplanations.a: Root credentials should not be shared; individual administrators should use separately managed identities.
distractorExplanations.c: Routine use increases exposure of the account's most privileged identity and is contrary to AWS root-user best practices.
distractorExplanations.d: Applications should never depend on unrestricted root credentials; use appropriately scoped roles or identities instead.

questions.hint: Root is an emergency/high-privilege identity, not a daily admin account.

questions.questionText: Why does AWS recommend that customers avoid creating access keys for the account root user?

options.text: Root access keys work only for read-only API calls
Root access keys can be used only from the AWS Management Console
Root access keys automatically expire after one hour
Root access keys are long-term programmatic credentials with unrestricted account privileges

questions.correctExplanation: Root access keys create a persistent programmatic path to unrestricted account privileges, so AWS recommends not creating them and using temporary, scoped credentials instead.

distractorExplanations.a: Root access keys inherit the root user's broad authority; they are not limited to read-only operations.
distractorExplanations.b: Access keys are intended for programmatic access, not interactive console sign-in.
distractorExplanations.c: They are long-term credentials unless explicitly removed, unlike temporary role credentials.

questions.hint: Think about the privilege level and lifetime of a root access key.

questions.questionText: A security team wants to identify supported AWS resources that are shared with principals outside its trusted AWS account or organization. Which IAM capability should it use?

options.text: IAM Access Analyzer external access analysis

questions.correctExplanation: IAM Access Analyzer can analyze supported resource-based policies and generate external access findings when resources in the chosen zone of trust are accessible by principals outside that trusted account or organization.

distractorExplanations.b: An IAM credential report summarizes the status of IAM user credentials such as passwords, access keys, and MFA; it does not analyze resource policies for external sharing.
distractorExplanations.c: The policy simulator evaluates how specified policies would authorize simulated requests; it does not continuously generate findings for resources shared outside a zone of trust.
distractorExplanations.d: An IAM password policy defines password requirements for IAM users; it does not discover resource access granted to external principals.

questions.hint: Think about discovering unintended external sharing.

questions.questionText: A company has decided to permanently close a standalone AWS account. Which identity must perform the account-closing action?
questions.correctExplanation: Closing an AWS account is one of the account-management tasks that requires signing in as the account root user.

distractorExplanations.a: IAM groups organize users and cannot themselves sign in or perform root-only account tasks.
distractorExplanations.c: Read-only permissions do not authorize closing an AWS account.
distractorExplanations.d: A workload role is not the account root user and cannot perform root-only account closure.

questions.hint: Some account-level actions cannot be delegated to ordinary IAM identities.

questions.questionText: Which TWO statements correctly describe IAM resource-based policies?

options.text: They can specify the principal that is allowed or denied access to the resource.
They are attached only to IAM users, groups, or roles.
They always replace the need for identity-based policies in every service.
They can never grant cross-account access.
They are attached directly to supported AWS resources.

questions.correctExplanation: Resource-based policies are attached to supported resources, such as an S3 bucket, and include a Principal element that identifies who can access the resource. They can also participate in cross-account authorization.

distractorExplanations.b: Policies attached to IAM identities are identity-based policies; resource-based policies are attached to supported resources.
distractorExplanations.c: Authorization can involve multiple policy types, and not every access pattern or service is handled exclusively by resource-based policies.
distractorExplanations.d: Many resource-based policies can name principals from another AWS account and are commonly used in cross-account access designs.

questions.hint: Where is the policy attached, and who can it name?

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes an IAM identity-based policy?

options.text: It is attached to an IAM identity such as a user, group, or role and defines what that identity can do
It is a TLS certificate used to authenticate websites
It determines the physical Region in which an identity can exist
It is attached directly to an S3 bucket and names external principals

questions.correctExplanation: Identity-based policies are attached to IAM users, groups, or roles and specify allowed or denied actions on resources for those identities.

distractorExplanations.b: TLS certificates are managed through services such as AWS Certificate Manager, not IAM identity policies.
distractorExplanations.c: IAM is a global service and policy attachment is not a Region placement control.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a resource-based policy, not an identity-based policy.

questions.hint: Identity-based means the policy follows the user, group, or role.

questions.questionText: An administrator wants to test how IAM policies would evaluate selected actions and resources without sending real requests to AWS services. Which IAM capability should be used?

options.text: IAM Access Analyzer external access findings

questions.correctExplanation: The IAM policy simulator evaluates policies against simulated actions and resources and returns whether the requests would be allowed or denied, without making real service requests.

distractorExplanations.a: AWS Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements, not IAM policy evaluation simulation.
distractorExplanations.b: A credential report summarizes IAM user credential status; it does not simulate authorization decisions.
distractorExplanations.d: External access analysis identifies supported resources shared outside a zone of trust; it is not an interactive request-authorization simulator.

questions.hint: Test authorization without performing the action.

questions.questionText: What is a defining characteristic of an IAM inline policy?

options.text: It is embedded directly in a single user, group, or role and has a one-to-one relationship with that identity
It is maintained globally by AWS and cannot be edited by the customer
It applies only to network traffic rules
It can be attached to an unlimited number of identities as a shared policy object

questions.correctExplanation: An inline policy is part of one specific IAM identity. It is useful when a strict one-to-one relationship between the policy and identity is desired.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS managed policies are maintained by AWS; inline policies are customer-defined within an identity.
distractorExplanations.c: IAM inline policies govern AWS authorization, not subnet or packet filtering.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a managed policy rather than an inline policy.

questions.hint: Inline means embedded inside one identity.

questions.questionText: Which IAM policy element is used to make a permission apply only under specified circumstances, such as when a request originates from a particular IP range or has a required resource tag?
questions.correctExplanation: The Condition element applies context-dependent tests to a policy statement, allowing permissions to depend on request attributes such as IP addresses, tags, dates, or authentication context.

distractorExplanations.a: Action identifies which API operations are covered, not the circumstances under which they apply.
distractorExplanations.b: Effect states whether the policy statement allows or denies; it does not define contextual requirements.
distractorExplanations.d: Resource identifies the objects to which the statement applies, not request context such as IP address or tags.

questions.hint: Which element adds an 'only if...' rule to a policy statement?

questions.questionText: In an IAM policy statement, what does the Effect element specify?

options.text: Which identity's password must be changed
Whether the statement allows or denies access
Which AWS Region will process the request
How long the API call may run

questions.correctExplanation: The Effect element has the authorization result for the statement—Allow or Deny—subject to the other policy elements and the overall policy evaluation logic.

distractorExplanations.a: Password management is unrelated to the Effect value.
distractorExplanations.c: Region selection is not the purpose of the Effect element.
distractorExplanations.d: IAM Effect controls authorization outcome, not operation runtime.

questions.hint: Effect answers: allow or deny?

questions.questionText: A developer assumes an IAM role and passes a session policy that is more restrictive than the role's identity-based permissions. How are the resulting session permissions determined?

options.text: The permissions are the union of the role policy and session policy, so either policy can independently grant access.
The session policy replaces all role permissions and can grant any action it names.
By the intersection of the role's identity-based permissions and the session policy
The role's identity-based policy always overrides and ignores the session policy.

questions.correctExplanation: Session policies can be passed when creating a temporary role session. They limit the session: effective permissions are the intersection of the IAM entity's identity-based permissions and the session policy, subject to other applicable policy types and explicit denies.

distractorExplanations.a: For this policy combination, effective permissions are constrained by the intersection rather than expanded by a union.
distractorExplanations.b: A session policy limits a role session; it cannot grant permissions beyond those already available through the role's applicable permissions.
distractorExplanations.d: Session policies participate in authorization and can restrict permissions that the role would otherwise have.

questions.hint: Session policies restrict temporary sessions; they do not expand the role.

questions.questionText: A company wants access permissions to scale automatically with projects by allowing a principal to access resources when the principal's project tag matches the resource's project tag. Which authorization approach is this?

options.text: Role-based access control based only on static job roles

questions.correctExplanation: AWS attribute-based access control defines permissions using attributes, which AWS represents with tags. Policies can allow actions when principal tags match resource tags, making permissions easier to scale as tagged resources and identities change.

distractorExplanations.b: Security groups control network traffic and do not implement IAM authorization by comparing principal and resource tags.
distractorExplanations.c: The root user has broad account authority and is unrelated to tag-based authorization between principals and resources.
distractorExplanations.d: Traditional RBAC bases permissions primarily on job function or role; the scenario specifically uses matching attributes or tags for dynamic authorization.

questions.hint: Matching tags are the key clue.

questions.questionText: For an IAM role, what is the purpose of the role's trust policy?

options.text: To store the role's console password
To specify which S3 objects are encrypted at rest
To define which principals are allowed to assume the role
To determine EC2 instance pricing for the role

questions.correctExplanation: A role trust policy is a resource-based policy on the role that specifies the principals that are trusted to call role-assumption operations and receive temporary credentials.

distractorExplanations.a: IAM roles do not have standard long-term passwords.
distractorExplanations.b: Encryption configuration is separate from the role trust relationship.
distractorExplanations.d: IAM authorization policies have no role in compute pricing.

questions.hint: Trust policy answers: who may assume this role?

questions.questionText: In AWS IAM Identity Center, what is a permission set used for?

options.text: To create a public DNS zone for workforce users
To encrypt every user password with a customer-managed KMS key
To configure VPC route tables for federated users
To define permissions that can be assigned to users or groups for access to one or more AWS accounts

questions.correctExplanation: Permission sets are collections of permission settings that IAM Identity Center provisions for assigned users or groups when they access AWS accounts.

distractorExplanations.a: DNS zones are a Route 53 function, not an IAM Identity Center function.
distractorExplanations.b: Permission sets define AWS account permissions; they are not password-encryption settings.
distractorExplanations.c: Network routing is unrelated to IAM Identity Center permission sets.

questions.hint: Think of a reusable package of AWS account permissions for workforce access.

questions.questionText: A consumer application needs a managed user directory that can handle user registration, sign-in, account recovery, and tokens for application authentication. Which Amazon Cognito feature is designed for this?
questions.correctExplanation: Cognito user pools are managed user directories for application users and provide registration, authentication, account-recovery, and token capabilities.

distractorExplanations.a: OUs group AWS accounts for governance and are unrelated to consumer application authentication.
distractorExplanations.c: Identity pools primarily provide federated identities and temporary AWS credentials rather than serving as the application's user directory.
distractorExplanations.d: CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules, not application user registration and sign-in.

questions.hint: User pool = application user directory.

questions.questionText: A mobile application allows guest users who have not signed in, but those guests still need narrowly scoped temporary AWS credentials to access permitted resources. Which Amazon Cognito capability supports this pattern?

options.text: Amazon Cognito identity pools with unauthenticated identities
AWS IAM user accounts created for every guest

questions.correctExplanation: Cognito identity pools can support unauthenticated guest identities and exchange those identities for temporary, limited AWS credentials associated with configured IAM roles.

distractorExplanations.b: Directory Service integrates directories such as Microsoft Active Directory; it is not the Cognito mechanism for guest application identities.
distractorExplanations.c: A user-pool password policy applies to users who authenticate through a user pool; it does not issue guest users temporary AWS credentials for AWS resources.
distractorExplanations.d: Creating long-term IAM users for transient application guests is not the Cognito pattern and would create unnecessary persistent credentials.

questions.hint: Guest access plus temporary AWS credentials points to identity pools.

questions.questionText: For an AWS KMS key, what is the primary function of the key policy?

options.text: To specify an S3 lifecycle transition schedule
To define Route 53 DNS routing behavior
To control access to the KMS key and define who can administer or use it
To choose the EC2 instance family used for encryption

questions.correctExplanation: Every KMS key has a key policy that is a primary mechanism for controlling who can manage the key and who can use it for cryptographic operations.

distractorExplanations.a: Lifecycle policies control object storage transitions, not access to KMS keys.
distractorExplanations.b: DNS routing is unrelated to KMS key authorization.
distractorExplanations.d: KMS key policies govern authorization, not compute instance selection.

questions.hint: The policy is attached to the key itself.

questions.questionText: A company requires direct control over a KMS key's policy, enable/disable state, rotation configuration, aliases, and deletion schedule. Which type of KMS key best matches this requirement?
questions.correctExplanation: Customer managed KMS keys are created in the customer's account and provide customer control over key policies, lifecycle, aliases, rotation options, and deletion scheduling.

distractorExplanations.a: A CloudFront cache key affects content caching behavior and is unrelated to cryptographic key lifecycle management.
distractorExplanations.b: AWS managed keys are created and managed by AWS services on the customer's behalf and offer less customer lifecycle control.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS owned keys are owned and managed by AWS and are not resources the customer directly administers.

questions.hint: Which KMS key type gives the customer the most direct lifecycle control?

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes an AWS managed KMS key?

options.text: It is a plaintext secret stored in IAM
It is created in the customer's account by an AWS service and its key policy and lifecycle are managed by AWS for that service
It is a key whose hardware security module is physically installed by the customer
It is always created manually by the customer and can be scheduled for deletion by the customer

questions.correctExplanation: AWS managed KMS keys are created on behalf of customers for integrated AWS services, while AWS controls key management details that customers would control for customer managed keys.

distractorExplanations.a: KMS keys are cryptographic key resources and are not plaintext IAM secrets.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes customer-controlled HSM scenarios, not an AWS managed KMS key.
distractorExplanations.d: Those are characteristics of customer managed KMS keys.

questions.hint: Managed by AWS for a service, but visible in the customer's account.

questions.questionText: A company wants AWS WAF to automatically identify a client that sends more than a configured number of requests in a time window and take an action such as block or count. Which WAF rule type is designed for this?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS WAF rate-based rules track request rates that match rule criteria and can apply actions when a source exceeds the configured rate limit.

distractorExplanations.a: KMS policies control cryptographic key access and do not count web requests.
distractorExplanations.b: S3 lifecycle rules transition or expire objects and do not filter web traffic.
distractorExplanations.d: A permissions boundary limits IAM identity permissions and does not inspect HTTP request rates.

questions.hint: Think request-rate threshold at the web application firewall.

questions.questionText: Which TWO types of request information can AWS WAF rules inspect when deciding whether to allow, block, or count a web request?

options.text: The physical serial number of the server rack
The EC2 host's CPU instruction set as a request field
IP address and request body characteristics

questions.correctExplanation: AWS WAF can evaluate characteristics of HTTP(S) requests, including IP addresses, headers, URI paths, query strings, and request bodies, then apply rule actions.

distractorExplanations.a: Billing information is not part of HTTP request inspection.
distractorExplanations.b: AWS WAF operates on web-request data and does not expose or evaluate data-center rack serial numbers.
distractorExplanations.c: CPU architecture is not web-request content that WAF rules inspect.

questions.hint: WAF sees web-request attributes, not billing or hardware metadata.

questions.questionText: Which statement accurately describes AWS Shield Standard?

options.text: It is a vulnerability scanner for operating-system packages
It is used to manage application user passwords
It is automatically included for AWS customers and provides protection against common network and transport layer DDoS attacks
It must be purchased separately for every EC2 instance

questions.correctExplanation: AWS Shield Standard is included automatically and provides baseline protection against common infrastructure-layer DDoS attacks for supported AWS resources.

distractorExplanations.a: Amazon Inspector provides vulnerability management; Shield focuses on DDoS protection.
distractorExplanations.b: Shield does not provide identity-management functionality.
distractorExplanations.d: Shield Standard protection is included rather than purchased per instance.

questions.hint: Baseline DDoS protection is included.

questions.questionText: A company with highly critical internet-facing applications wants enhanced DDoS protections beyond the baseline service, including access to specialized DDoS response expertise. Which option should it evaluate?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Shield Advanced adds enhanced DDoS protections and support capabilities for customers that need stronger protections for critical applications.

distractorExplanations.b: Macie discovers sensitive data in S3; it does not provide DDoS response support.
distractorExplanations.c: Directory Service provides managed directory capabilities, not network-attack mitigation.
distractorExplanations.d: Artifact supplies compliance reports and agreements, not enhanced DDoS response services.

questions.hint: Look for the premium DDoS protection tier.

questions.questionText: What does enabling a security standard in AWS Security Hub primarily add beyond simply collecting findings from other services?

options.text: A private physical network connection to AWS
Automated security checks against the controls defined by that standard
Automatic replacement of every noncompliant resource
Automatic purchase of third-party security software

questions.correctExplanation: Security Hub standards contain controls that run automated checks against supported AWS resources and produce control findings and compliance status.

distractorExplanations.a: Dedicated networking is provided by services such as Direct Connect, not Security Hub standards.
distractorExplanations.c: Security Hub identifies findings and control status; remediation depends on configured workflows or separate actions.
distractorExplanations.d: Security Hub standards perform control checks; they do not purchase Marketplace products.

questions.hint: Standards add control checks, not just finding aggregation.

questions.questionText: A compliance analyst needs to see how the configuration of an AWS resource changed over time, including earlier configuration states and relationships. Which AWS Config capability provides this information?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Config records configuration items over time, allowing customers to review historical resource configurations and relationships in addition to evaluating rules.

distractorExplanations.a: The requested capability concerns tracked AWS resource configurations rather than just IAM password rules.
distractorExplanations.b: CloudFront caching improves content delivery and does not record AWS resource configuration history.
distractorExplanations.d: Spot notices relate to compute capacity interruptions, not configuration history.

questions.hint: Think historical snapshots of resource configuration.

questions.questionText: Without creating a trail, how much recent management-event history can a user typically view in AWS CloudTrail Event history?

options.text: No history is available until an S3 bucket is configured

questions.correctExplanation: CloudTrail Event history provides a searchable record of the past 90 days of management events in an AWS Region without requiring the customer to create a trail.

distractorExplanations.a: Long-term retention requires configuring a trail or other storage/analytics options; Event history is not a seven-year archive.
distractorExplanations.b: CloudTrail Event history retains a substantially longer recent history of management events.
distractorExplanations.d: CloudTrail Event history is available for recent management events even without creating a trail.

questions.hint: Think recent built-in history, not long-term archival.

questions.questionText: A company needs an ongoing CloudTrail record delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket for longer-term retention and analysis. What should it create?
questions.correctExplanation: A CloudTrail trail can continuously deliver selected CloudTrail events to an S3 bucket, enabling retention beyond the built-in Event history window and integration with analysis workflows.

distractorExplanations.b: Hosted zones store DNS records, not API audit logs.
distractorExplanations.c: Placement groups influence instance placement and are unrelated to audit-log delivery.
distractorExplanations.d: IAM groups organize user permissions and do not deliver audit events to S3.

questions.hint: Event history is temporary; a trail creates ongoing delivery.

questions.questionText: An enterprise wants one CloudTrail configuration that records events for all current and future accounts in its AWS Organization. Which feature is designed for this?

options.text: A security group shared with AWS RAM
A local trail created separately by an IAM user in one member account

questions.correctExplanation: An organization trail is created for an AWS Organization and can apply CloudTrail logging to all member accounts, including accounts added later.

distractorExplanations.a: Security groups control network traffic; sharing one does not create organization-wide API auditing.
distractorExplanations.b: A bucket ACL controls object access and does not configure CloudTrail across an organization.
distractorExplanations.d: A single-account trail does not automatically govern every current and future organization account.

questions.hint: Think one trail governed at the organization level.

questions.questionText: A legal team needs to review and accept an AWS agreement, such as an eligible business associate agreement, through a self-service AWS portal. Which AWS Artifact capability is intended for this?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Artifact Agreements lets authorized users review, accept, and manage eligible agreements with AWS through a self-service workflow.

distractorExplanations.a: Inspector reports software vulnerabilities, not contractual agreements.
distractorExplanations.b: Artifact Reports provides audit and compliance reports; Agreements is the capability for reviewing and accepting eligible agreements.
distractorExplanations.c: Shield Advanced is a DDoS protection service and does not manage legal agreements.

questions.hint: Artifact has both reports and agreements; this question is about contracts.

questions.questionText: A company is evaluating whether a particular AWS service can be used for a workload subject to a specific compliance program. Which TWO actions are appropriate?

options.text: Check whether the AWS service is listed as in scope for the relevant compliance program
Assume AWS certification removes all customer compliance responsibilities
Assume that every AWS service is automatically covered by every AWS compliance program
Evaluate and configure the customer's own use of the service to meet the customer's compliance obligations
Select an AWS Region only by price and ignore regulatory requirements

questions.correctExplanation: AWS publishes service-in-scope information for compliance programs, but customers still must evaluate their own requirements and securely configure and use the selected services under the shared responsibility model.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS compliance of the cloud does not eliminate the customer's responsibility for its data, configuration, and use of services.
distractorExplanations.c: Compliance program scope varies by service and program, so customers must verify coverage.
distractorExplanations.e: Location and regulatory requirements can affect compliance decisions and should not be ignored.

questions.hint: Verify service scope, then address your own compliance responsibilities.

questions.questionText: A data engineering team needs a serverless data integration service to discover data, maintain a centralized Data Catalog, and run ETL jobs that prepare data for analytics. Which AWS service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Glue is a serverless data integration service that includes a Data Catalog and capabilities to discover, prepare, transform, and move data for analytics and machine learning.

distractorExplanations.a: Cognito provides application identity capabilities, not data integration.
distractorExplanations.b: Shield provides DDoS protection, not ETL processing.
distractorExplanations.c: Route 53 provides DNS and traffic routing, not ETL or data cataloging.

questions.hint: Think ETL plus a shared data catalog.

questions.questionText: A company wants a managed service for indexing, searching, and analyzing large volumes of application logs and operational data using OpenSearch APIs and dashboards. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service is a managed service for deploying, operating, and scaling OpenSearch clusters used for search, log analytics, observability, and related use cases.

distractorExplanations.a: EFS is shared file storage and does not provide a managed search and analytics engine.
distractorExplanations.b: AWS Backup centralizes backups but does not index and search operational logs.
distractorExplanations.d: SES is an email service, not a search analytics platform.

questions.hint: Think managed search and log analytics.

questions.questionText: Business users need interactive dashboards and self-service business intelligence to visualize and analyze company data. Which AWS service is designed for this?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon Quick Sight, the business intelligence capability within Amazon Quick, provides interactive dashboards, visualizations, ad hoc analysis, and embedded analytics.

distractorExplanations.a: SQS queues messages between application components and does not provide BI dashboards.
distractorExplanations.b: Route 53 is a DNS service, not a business intelligence platform.
distractorExplanations.d: CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules, not analytics visualization.

questions.hint: Think dashboards and BI, not data processing infrastructure.

questions.questionText: Which TWO capabilities are provided by Amazon EventBridge?

options.text: It requires customers to provision and manage event-bus servers.
It provides persistent block storage volumes for EC2 instances.
It is primarily a managed relational database engine.
It can use rules to route matching events to selected targets.
It can receive events from AWS services, custom applications, and supported SaaS sources.

questions.correctExplanation: Amazon EventBridge is a serverless event bus that accepts events from AWS services, custom applications, and supported SaaS integrations and evaluates rules to route matching events to targets.

distractorExplanations.a: EventBridge is a serverless event bus; customers do not provision event-bus servers.
distractorExplanations.b: Amazon EBS provides EC2 block storage; EventBridge is an event-routing service.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon RDS and Aurora provide managed relational databases; EventBridge is not a database.

questions.hint: Think event sources plus event routing.

questions.questionText: A serverless application has a multi-step process with branching, retries, waits, and calls to several AWS services. Which service should orchestrate the workflow?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Step Functions coordinates distributed applications using state machines, with built-in support for sequencing, branching, retries, error handling, and service integrations.

distractorExplanations.a: KMS manages encryption keys, not application workflow state.
distractorExplanations.b: CloudFront caches and delivers content; it does not orchestrate application workflow steps.
distractorExplanations.d: ECR stores container images and does not coordinate multi-step workflows.

questions.hint: Think state machine orchestration.

questions.questionText: A company wants a cloud-based contact center that can handle customer voice and chat interactions without operating traditional call-center infrastructure. Which AWS service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon Connect is a managed cloud contact-center service for customer interactions such as voice and chat, reducing the need to deploy and maintain traditional contact-center systems.

distractorExplanations.a: S3 stores objects and does not provide a contact-center platform.
distractorExplanations.b: CodeBuild compiles and tests software; it is not a customer contact center.
distractorExplanations.c: VPC provides virtual networking, not contact-center functionality.

questions.hint: Think customer contact center.

questions.questionText: An application needs a managed service to send transactional and marketing email at scale using APIs or SMTP. Which AWS service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon SES is a scalable email service that applications can use through APIs or SMTP to send transactional, marketing, and other email.

distractorExplanations.a: SQS stores messages in queues and does not deliver email to internet recipients.
distractorExplanations.b: Step Functions orchestrates workflows and is not an email delivery service.
distractorExplanations.c: SNS can send notifications to multiple endpoints, but SES is purpose-built for high-scale email sending and receiving workflows.

questions.hint: Purpose-built AWS email delivery service.

questions.questionText: Which TWO tasks are core capabilities of AWS CodeBuild?

options.text: Registering and routing internet domain names.
Compiling source code and running build commands or tests in managed build environments.
Producing build artifacts without requiring the customer to maintain build servers.

questions.correctExplanation: AWS CodeBuild is a fully managed continuous integration service that runs build commands such as compilation and tests and can produce deployable artifacts, while AWS manages the build infrastructure.

distractorExplanations.a: Amazon Route 53 provides domain registration and DNS routing; CodeBuild is a build service.
distractorExplanations.b: Amazon WorkSpaces provides managed virtual desktops; CodeBuild is a continuous-integration build service.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon S3 Glacier storage classes handle long-term archival; CodeBuild does not provide archival storage.

questions.hint: Think managed build servers: compile, test, package.

questions.questionText: A team wants to model and automate a software release process with source, build, test, approval, and deployment stages. Which AWS service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS CodePipeline is a continuous delivery service for modeling and automating the stages and actions required to release software.

distractorExplanations.a: Inspector scans supported workloads for vulnerabilities and does not orchestrate releases.
distractorExplanations.c: CodeBuild runs builds and tests but does not by itself model the entire multi-stage release pipeline.
distractorExplanations.d: Storage Gateway connects on-premises environments to AWS storage, not software delivery pipelines.

questions.hint: Think CI/CD pipeline orchestration.

questions.questionText: Developers need to trace a single user request as it travels through multiple services in a distributed application to identify latency and errors. Which AWS service is designed for this?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS X-Ray collects trace data about requests as they move through distributed applications, helping developers analyze service maps, latency, and errors.

distractorExplanations.b: CloudTrail records AWS API activity for governance and auditing rather than tracing application requests end to end.
distractorExplanations.c: Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements, not application traces.
distractorExplanations.d: Route 53 provides DNS routing and does not trace distributed application calls.

questions.hint: Think distributed tracing.

questions.questionText: A company wants to stream existing desktop applications from AWS to users' devices without rewriting the applications or installing them locally. Which service best fits?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon WorkSpaces Applications, formerly AppStream 2.0, is a fully managed application-streaming service that delivers desktop applications to users without requiring application rewrites or local installation.

distractorExplanations.a: Lambda runs event-driven code and does not present interactive desktop applications to end users.
distractorExplanations.c: Secure Browser provides hosted browser sessions for web resources, not general streaming of existing desktop applications.
distractorExplanations.d: S3 can store application installers but does not stream interactive desktop applications.

questions.hint: Stream applications, not a whole persistent desktop.

questions.questionText: An organization wants fully managed persistent virtual desktops in AWS for employees who need a desktop environment that they can access remotely. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon WorkSpaces provides managed cloud desktops that users can access from supported devices, reducing the need to manage traditional physical or virtual desktop infrastructure.

distractorExplanations.a: ECR stores container images and does not provide end-user desktops.
distractorExplanations.b: API Gateway publishes APIs and does not provide desktop-as-a-service.
distractorExplanations.c: Batch runs compute jobs and does not deliver interactive desktop sessions.

questions.hint: Think desktop as a service.

questions.questionText: Remote employees need secure browser-based access to internal websites and SaaS applications, but they do not require a full virtual desktop. Which service is the most direct fit?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser is a managed hosted-browser service that provides controlled access to private websites, SaaS applications, and the internet without requiring a full desktop.

distractorExplanations.a: Client VPN provides network connectivity, but it does not itself provide an isolated hosted browser session.
distractorExplanations.b: WorkSpaces Applications streams desktop applications; Secure Browser is specifically designed for hosted browser access to web resources.
distractorExplanations.d: CloudFront distributes content to users and does not create secure enterprise browser sessions.

questions.hint: Only the browser experience is needed.

questions.questionText: A frontend team wants a managed platform to build, deploy, and host web and mobile application frontends while integrating with AWS backend capabilities. Which service should it evaluate?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Amplify provides tools and managed workflows for building, deploying, and hosting web and mobile application frontends with integrations to AWS backend services.

distractorExplanations.a: Shield provides DDoS protection rather than frontend build and hosting workflows.
distractorExplanations.b: Neptune is a graph database, not a frontend web/mobile service.
distractorExplanations.d: Snowball transfers large datasets using physical devices; it is not a frontend development platform.

questions.hint: Think frontend and mobile development.

questions.questionText: A manufacturer needs managed cloud connectivity so millions of IoT devices can securely publish telemetry and receive messages using IoT protocols. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS IoT Core securely connects IoT devices to AWS and supports device communication and messaging at scale without customers operating their own message infrastructure.

distractorExplanations.a: Redshift is a data warehouse and does not manage device connectivity.
distractorExplanations.b: Service Catalog distributes approved cloud products rather than connecting physical devices.
distractorExplanations.d: SES sends email and is not an IoT device messaging service.

questions.hint: Think device-to-cloud connectivity.

questions.questionText: A company wants to analyze customer reviews to identify sentiment, key phrases, entities, and language using a prebuilt natural-language processing service. Which AWS service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon Comprehend is a natural-language processing service that can detect sentiment, entities, key phrases, language, and other insights from text.

distractorExplanations.a: Polly converts text to speech and does not extract sentiment or entities from text.
distractorExplanations.c: Rekognition analyzes images and video, not text sentiment.
distractorExplanations.d: Textract extracts text and structured data from documents but does not primarily perform NLP sentiment analysis.

questions.hint: Think NLP insights from text.

questions.questionText: An accessibility feature needs to convert written text into lifelike spoken audio. Which AWS service is designed for this?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon Polly is a text-to-speech service that turns text into natural-sounding spoken audio.

distractorExplanations.b: Transcribe performs the opposite direction by converting speech to text.
distractorExplanations.c: Kinesis handles streaming data and does not generate speech.
distractorExplanations.d: Translate converts text between languages but does not synthesize speech.

questions.hint: Text in, speech out.

questions.questionText: A software engineer wants a generative-AI assistant that can answer questions about AWS, help understand and operate AWS workloads, and assist with software development tasks. Which AWS offering is designed for this?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon Q includes generative-AI assistants such as Amazon Q Developer that help users understand, build, extend, and operate AWS applications and perform software-development tasks.

distractorExplanations.a: SQS is a message queue and does not provide conversational AI assistance.
distractorExplanations.b: Direct Connect is dedicated networking, not a generative-AI assistant.
distractorExplanations.d: Macie discovers sensitive data in S3 and is not a generative-AI assistant.

questions.hint: Think AWS's generative-AI work assistant.

questions.questionText: A media application needs a managed AI service to detect objects, scenes, faces, and other visual information in images and videos. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon Rekognition provides prebuilt computer-vision capabilities for analyzing images and videos, including detecting visual objects and features.

distractorExplanations.a: Polly synthesizes speech from text and does not perform computer vision.
distractorExplanations.b: Comprehend analyzes natural-language text rather than images and video.
distractorExplanations.d: Glue integrates and transforms data but is not a computer-vision service.

questions.hint: Think computer vision.

questions.questionText: An insurance company needs to extract printed text, form fields, and tables from scanned documents without manually building OCR pipelines. Which AWS service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon Textract uses machine learning to extract text, handwriting, forms, and tables from scanned documents and images.

distractorExplanations.a: OpenSearch can index text after extraction but does not primarily perform document OCR and form extraction.
distractorExplanations.c: SNS distributes notifications and does not extract document content.
distractorExplanations.d: Transcribe converts audio speech to text, not scanned document content.

questions.hint: Think document text and form extraction.

questions.questionText: A call-recording application needs automatic speech recognition to convert audio conversations into text transcripts. Which AWS service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon Transcribe is an automatic speech recognition service that converts speech in audio or video into text.

distractorExplanations.a: Translate changes text from one language to another and does not transcribe audio.
distractorExplanations.c: Polly converts text into speech rather than speech into text.
distractorExplanations.d: Athena runs SQL queries on data and does not perform speech recognition.

questions.hint: Speech in, text out.

questions.questionText: A global website needs a managed service to automatically translate text content between supported human languages. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: Amazon Translate is a neural machine translation service for translating text between supported languages.

distractorExplanations.a: CloudFormation provisions infrastructure from templates and does not translate content.
distractorExplanations.c: Comprehend analyzes text for meaning and sentiment but is not primarily a translation service.
distractorExplanations.d: Polly converts text to audio, not one language to another.

questions.hint: Language A to language B.

questions.questionText: A company wants recommendations that identify over-provisioned or under-provisioned AWS resources by analyzing utilization metrics so it can improve price-performance. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes utilization and configuration data and recommends resource options that can improve performance and cost efficiency for supported AWS resources.

distractorExplanations.a: CloudHSM provides dedicated cryptographic hardware, not utilization recommendations.
distractorExplanations.c: Artifact provides compliance documents rather than resource-sizing recommendations.
distractorExplanations.d: Route 53 provides DNS and health checking, not rightsizing analysis.

questions.hint: Think automated rightsizing recommendations.

questions.questionText: A company uses commercial software licenses with limits based on cores, sockets, or instances and wants centralized rules and usage tracking across AWS and on-premises environments. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS License Manager helps organizations configure license rules and track consumption of software licenses across AWS and supported on-premises environments.

distractorExplanations.a: GuardDuty detects threats and does not manage software licensing.
distractorExplanations.b: Cost Explorer analyzes spend but does not enforce software license-consumption rules.
distractorExplanations.d: CodePipeline automates software releases and does not track license entitlements.

questions.hint: Think license entitlement and consumption tracking.

questions.questionText: An IT organization wants to give internal teams a catalog of approved, preconfigured cloud products that users can provision without designing each product from scratch. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Service Catalog lets organizations create and govern catalogs of approved IT services and cloud products that end users can provision in a controlled way.

distractorExplanations.b: CloudFront is a CDN and not an internal cloud-product catalog.
distractorExplanations.c: Marketplace is a catalog for purchasing software and services; Service Catalog is for an organization's own governed catalog of approved cloud products.
distractorExplanations.d: Inspector finds software vulnerabilities and does not distribute approved infrastructure products.

questions.hint: Internal catalog of approved cloud products.

questions.questionText: An administrator needs to view the current limits for AWS resources in an account and request increases for adjustable limits. Which service should the administrator use?
questions.correctExplanation: Service Quotas provides a central place to view AWS service quotas, monitor usage against some quotas, and request increases for adjustable quotas.

distractorExplanations.a: X-Ray traces application requests and does not manage quotas.
distractorExplanations.b: Budgets tracks cost and usage thresholds, not technical service limits.
distractorExplanations.c: Glacier provides archival storage and does not manage account service limits.

questions.hint: Think service limits.

questions.questionText: Which TWO capabilities are associated with AWS Systems Manager?

options.text: Replacing every operating system with an AWS-managed operating system.
Providing a global content delivery network at edge locations.
Serving as the authoritative DNS service for public domain names.
Running operational commands or automations across managed nodes.
Managing inventory and patching for supported managed nodes across AWS and hybrid environments.

questions.correctExplanation: AWS Systems Manager provides centralized operational capabilities for managed nodes, including Run Command and Automation as well as inventory and patch-management features across AWS and supported hybrid environments.

distractorExplanations.a: Systems Manager helps operate supported systems but does not replace their operating systems.
distractorExplanations.b: Amazon CloudFront is the CDN; Systems Manager does not cache content at edge locations.
distractorExplanations.c: Amazon Route 53 provides authoritative DNS; Systems Manager is an operations-management service.

questions.hint: Think fleet operations, not application traffic.

questions.questionText: An architecture team wants an AWS console tool that stores workload reviews and evaluates workloads against the AWS Well-Architected Framework's pillars and best practices. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: The AWS Well-Architected Tool helps teams document workloads, answer framework questions, identify risks, and track improvement plans against Well-Architected best practices.

distractorExplanations.b: Pricing Calculator estimates architecture cost but does not conduct Well-Architected reviews.
distractorExplanations.c: DMS migrates database data and does not perform architecture reviews.
distractorExplanations.d: CloudTrail records API activity and does not assess architecture against Well-Architected questions.

questions.hint: Think the console implementation of Well-Architected reviews.

questions.questionText: Before migrating, a company wants to collect inventory, configuration, and dependency information about its on-premises servers to better understand the environment. Which AWS service is designed for this discovery phase?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Application Discovery Service collects information about on-premises servers and applications to support migration planning and dependency analysis.

distractorExplanations.a: CloudFront is a CDN and does not inventory on-premises servers.
distractorExplanations.b: KMS manages cryptographic keys and does not collect server discovery data.
distractorExplanations.d: Application Migration Service replicates and migrates servers; discovery focuses on inventory and dependency information before migration.

questions.hint: Discovery before migration.
