questions.questionText: A company wants to lift and shift physical, virtual, or cloud-based servers to AWS with continuous block-level replication and automated conversion for launch on AWS. Which service should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Application Migration Service is designed to simplify lift-and-shift server migrations by continuously replicating source servers and preparing them to launch on AWS.

distractorExplanations.a: Glue integrates and transforms data for analytics, not server migration.
distractorExplanations.b: WorkSpaces provides managed desktops rather than migrating existing servers.
distractorExplanations.c: AWS SCT converts database schemas; it does not perform whole-server lift-and-shift migrations.

questions.hint: Think server migration rather than database-only migration.

questions.questionText: An organization wants a data-driven business case for moving on-premises workloads to AWS, including inventory analysis and projected cost comparisons. Which AWS offering should it use?
questions.correctExplanation: Migration Evaluator analyzes environment data to help organizations build a migration business case and estimate potential cost and infrastructure benefits of moving to AWS.

distractorExplanations.a: CloudHSM provides cryptographic hardware and does not evaluate migration TCO.
distractorExplanations.b: WAF filters web requests and does not build migration business cases.
distractorExplanations.d: SQS provides message queues and does not analyze migration economics.

questions.hint: Think migration assessment and business case.

questions.questionText: A large migration uses several AWS and partner migration tools. The program manager wants one place to track application migration status and progress across those tools. Which service should be used?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Migration Hub provides centralized visibility into migration progress and can aggregate status from supported migration tools and applications.

distractorExplanations.a: Shield protects against DDoS attacks and does not track migrations.
distractorExplanations.b: EventBridge routes application events and is not a migration tracking dashboard.
distractorExplanations.c: Security Hub centralizes security posture and findings, not migration progress.

questions.hint: One place to track a migration program.

questions.questionText: A branch office needs an encrypted network connection between its on-premises network and an Amazon VPC over the public internet. Which AWS connectivity option is designed for this?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Site-to-Site VPN creates encrypted IPsec tunnels between an on-premises network and AWS over the internet.

distractorExplanations.a: CloudFront is a content delivery network and does not connect private networks.
distractorExplanations.c: Client VPN connects individual remote clients rather than creating a site-to-site connection between networks.
distractorExplanations.d: Direct Connect uses a dedicated network connection rather than an encrypted tunnel over the public internet.

questions.hint: Network-to-network encrypted VPN.

questions.questionText: Remote employees need secure VPN connectivity from individual laptops to resources in AWS and an on-premises network. Which managed AWS service is intended for client-based remote access?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Client VPN is a managed client-based VPN service that allows individual users to securely connect from supported devices to AWS and connected networks.

distractorExplanations.b: Route 53 provides DNS and does not establish remote-access VPN sessions.
distractorExplanations.c: Site-to-Site VPN connects networks to each other and is not the client-based remote-user service.
distractorExplanations.d: Transit Gateway provides network transit routing but does not by itself provide end-user VPN client sessions.

questions.hint: User device to network, not network to network.

questions.questionText: A company needs EC2 instances to run on single-tenant hardware but does not need visibility into the physical host or control over instance placement. Which EC2 tenancy option best fits?

options.text: Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances with default tenancy

questions.correctExplanation: Dedicated Instances run on hardware dedicated to a single AWS account while abstracting the physical host; customers do not get host IDs, socket/core visibility, targeted placement, or host affinity.

distractorExplanations.a: Dedicated Hosts provide a fully dedicated physical server with host visibility, placement control, and host affinity, which are more capabilities than the scenario requires.
distractorExplanations.b: Default-tenancy On-Demand Instances can run on hardware shared with other AWS accounts.
distractorExplanations.d: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity and can be interrupted; they do not by themselves provide single-tenant dedicated hardware.

questions.hint: Look for dedicated hardware without host-level control.

questions.questionText: Which TWO statements correctly distinguish regional and zonal Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances?

options.text: A regional Reserved Instance always reserves EC2 capacity in every Availability Zone in its Region.
Regional Reserved Instances and zonal Reserved Instances have different term lengths by definition.
A regional Reserved Instance discount can apply to eligible instance usage in any Availability Zone in the specified Region.
A zonal Reserved Instance provides Availability Zone flexibility across the entire Region.
A zonal Reserved Instance reserves capacity in the specified Availability Zone.

questions.correctExplanation: A zonal Reserved Instance both provides the RI billing benefit and reserves capacity in one specified Availability Zone. A regional Reserved Instance does not reserve capacity, but its discount can apply to eligible usage across Availability Zones in the Region.

distractorExplanations.a: Regional Reserved Instances provide a billing discount but do not reserve capacity.
distractorExplanations.b: Scope affects capacity reservation and flexibility; it does not define a different RI term length.
distractorExplanations.d: A zonal Reserved Instance is scoped to one specified Availability Zone and does not provide Availability Zone flexibility.

questions.hint: Think capacity reservation versus Availability Zone flexibility.

questions.questionText: An application frequently transfers data between EC2 instances located in different Availability Zones within the same AWS Region. Which pricing consideration should the architect include?

options.text: Cross-Availability-Zone transfer is charged only if the instances use Spot pricing.
Cross-Availability-Zone data transfer can incur regional data-transfer charges.
Cross-Availability-Zone transfer requires a Reserved Instance before any data can flow.
All EC2 data transfer within an AWS Region is always free.

questions.correctExplanation: EC2 traffic that crosses Availability Zones within the same AWS Region can incur regional data-transfer charges. Architects should include that traffic pattern when estimating the cost of highly available multi-AZ designs.

distractorExplanations.a: Data-transfer pricing is independent of whether the instances use Spot, On-Demand, or another EC2 purchasing option.
distractorExplanations.c: Reserved Instances are a pricing-discount mechanism and are not required for network traffic between Availability Zones.
distractorExplanations.d: Transfers within the same Availability Zone can be free in relevant cases, but cross-Availability-Zone transfers for EC2 can incur regional data-transfer charges.

questions.hint: High availability can introduce network-transfer cost between zones.

questions.questionText: A company expects to transfer data from the internet into Amazon EC2. Which statement best reflects the general AWS pricing model for this traffic?

options.text: Data transfer into Amazon EC2 from the internet is generally priced at no additional data-transfer charge.
Inbound data transfer is billed only when the EC2 instance uses an Elastic IP address.
Inbound internet traffic requires a Savings Plan to avoid data-transfer charges.
All inbound internet traffic is charged at the same rate as outbound internet traffic.

questions.correctExplanation: AWS generally does not charge for data transfer into Amazon EC2 from the internet. Other transfer paths, such as certain cross-Availability-Zone or outbound internet traffic, can have separate charges.

distractorExplanations.b: Whether an Elastic IP address is used is not the general basis for charging internet data transfer into EC2.
distractorExplanations.c: Savings Plans discount eligible compute usage; they are not a prerequisite for the general inbound data-transfer pricing treatment.
distractorExplanations.d: AWS data-transfer pricing generally treats inbound and outbound internet traffic differently; outbound traffic commonly has tiered charges after applicable free allowances.

questions.hint: Remember the usual direction that AWS makes free.

questions.questionText: A workload sends a large amount of data from AWS services to users on the public internet. Which cost characteristic should the architect consider?

options.text: All data transfer out to the internet is always free regardless of volume.
Data transfer out to the internet can incur tiered charges after applicable free data-transfer allowances.
Internet data transfer out is included only when using Reserved Instances.
Outbound internet transfer is charged only when data leaves an AWS Region through Direct Connect.

questions.correctExplanation: AWS aggregates eligible data transfer out to the internet across many services for tiered pricing and provides an applicable monthly free allowance; usage beyond that can incur data-transfer charges.

distractorExplanations.a: AWS provides applicable free allowances, but outbound internet transfer can incur charges beyond them.
distractorExplanations.c: Reserved Instances affect eligible EC2 compute pricing, not whether internet egress is charged.
distractorExplanations.d: Direct Connect has its own pricing; ordinary internet egress can also incur data-transfer charges.

questions.hint: Think about egress rather than ingress.

questions.questionText: A compliance archive will be retained for years and accessed less than once per year. The company prioritizes the lowest storage cost and can wait hours for retrieval. Which S3 storage class is designed for this use case?
questions.correctExplanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is AWS's lowest-cost S3 storage option for long-lived archive data accessed less than once a year. Objects are archived and must be restored before access, with retrieval measured in hours.

distractorExplanations.b: S3 Express One Zone is designed for high-performance, low-latency access in a single Availability Zone, not lowest-cost long-term archival.
distractorExplanations.c: S3 Standard is designed for frequently accessed data and has higher storage cost than archival classes.
distractorExplanations.d: S3 Standard-IA provides millisecond access for infrequently accessed data, but it is not AWS's lowest-cost class for long-lived archives accessed less than annually.

questions.hint: Lowest cost, longest-lived archive, slow retrieval.

questions.questionText: Which TWO pricing characteristics of Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering should a customer understand when evaluating it for data with unknown or changing access patterns?

options.text: Every object is permanently kept in the Frequent Access tier.
It has no data retrieval fees for the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class.
It requires a one-year commitment for every object stored in the class.
It charges a small monitoring and automation fee for eligible objects.
Objects incur a mandatory 180-day minimum storage duration in the standard Intelligent-Tiering class.

questions.correctExplanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering uses a small monitoring and automation charge for eligible objects to automatically adjust storage tiers as access patterns change. The class does not charge data retrieval fees, which is an important difference from several infrequent-access and archive storage classes.

distractorExplanations.a: Eligible objects are automatically moved among access tiers based on observed access patterns, which is the core cost-optimization behavior of the class.
distractorExplanations.c: S3 Intelligent-Tiering does not impose an account-level or per-object one-year contractual commitment.
distractorExplanations.e: S3 Intelligent-Tiering itself has no minimum storage duration; 180-day duration considerations apply to specific archival storage such as S3 Glacier Deep Archive, not the base Intelligent-Tiering class.

questions.hint: Look at automation overhead versus retrieval charges.

questions.questionText: Which AWS Support plan is automatically available to every AWS customer and includes 24/7 access to account and billing assistance, support forums, service health checks, and documentation?
questions.correctExplanation: Basic Support is automatically available to all AWS customers. It includes account and billing assistance, support forums, service health checks, and AWS documentation and best-practice resources.

distractorExplanations.b: Unified Operations is a higher-level paid support offering and is not automatically included with every AWS account.
distractorExplanations.c: Business Support+ is a paid plan that adds technical support features such as 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers.
distractorExplanations.d: Enterprise Support is a paid plan with additional proactive capabilities, including a designated Technical Account Manager.

questions.hint: Which support level comes with every account?

questions.questionText: Which TWO features are included with AWS Business Support+ according to the current AWS Support offering?

options.text: All AWS service usage becomes free while the support plan is active.
AWS assumes responsibility for configuring the customer's applications.
24/7 phone, web, and chat access to Cloud Support Engineers
Real-time contextual responses through generative AI
A designated Technical Account Manager is included with every Business Support+ account.

questions.correctExplanation: Business Support+ includes 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers through phone, web, and chat and adds real-time contextual responses through generative AI. Enterprise Support adds benefits such as a designated TAM.

distractorExplanations.a: A support subscription does not eliminate charges for AWS service consumption.
distractorExplanations.b: Support engineers advise customers; the customer retains responsibility for configuring and operating its workloads under the shared responsibility model.
distractorExplanations.e: A designated TAM is an Enterprise Support benefit, not a standard Business Support+ feature.

questions.hint: Use the current 2026 support-plan feature set.

questions.questionText: A company discovers suspicious traffic originating from AWS infrastructure and believes AWS resources are being used for malware distribution. Which AWS team is the appropriate destination for an abuse report?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS directs reports of suspected abuse of AWS resources, including malware distribution and spam, to the AWS Trust & Safety team.

distractorExplanations.a: Professional Services provides consulting and implementation expertise; it is not the abuse-reporting function.
distractorExplanations.b: Documentation feedback channels are for documentation issues and are explicitly not the destination for AWS abuse reports.
distractorExplanations.d: Billing Support handles account and billing questions, not reports of abusive use of AWS resources.

questions.hint: Think about the AWS function responsible for abuse reports.

questions.questionText: An enterprise wants AWS experts to work directly with its teams on a complex migration and modernization program. Which AWS resource is designed to provide consulting and hands-on cloud expertise?
questions.correctExplanation: AWS Professional Services provides AWS expertise for customer transformation initiatives such as migrations, modernization, data and AI, and other complex cloud programs.

distractorExplanations.a: AWS Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements, not implementation consulting.
distractorExplanations.c: The Free Tier provides limited free service usage offers; it is not a consulting organization.
distractorExplanations.d: The Cost and Usage Report provides granular billing data, not professional consulting services.

questions.hint: Look for AWS consulting expertise, not technical support cases.

questions.questionText: Which TWO statements about AWS Health are correct for AWS customers?

options.text: The AWS Health Dashboard is available to all AWS customers at no additional cost and requires no setup.
AWS Health is primarily a tool for estimating the monthly cost of proposed architectures.
Only Enterprise Support customers can view the AWS Health Dashboard.
Eligible paid support plans can use the AWS Health API to programmatically integrate AWS Health event information with other systems.
The AWS Health API replaces IAM authentication and can be called anonymously.

questions.correctExplanation: All AWS customers can use the AWS Health Dashboard without additional cost or setup. Customers on eligible paid support plans can also use the AWS Health API to retrieve health information programmatically and integrate it with internal or third-party systems.

distractorExplanations.b: AWS Pricing Calculator estimates architecture costs; AWS Health provides visibility into events that can affect AWS services and resources.
distractorExplanations.c: The AWS Health Dashboard is available to all AWS customers; paid support is not required just to use the dashboard.
distractorExplanations.e: AWS Health API requests require authenticated, signed requests and eligibility under supported AWS Support plans.

questions.hint: Separate the universally available dashboard from programmatic API access.
